es.definition: El cloro libre es la concentración de cloro activo y no combinado disponible en el agua de la piscina para sanitizar y desinfectar.
es.explanation: El cloro libre existe en dos formas: ácido hipocloroso (HOCl) e ion hipoclorito (OCl-). El ácido hipocloroso es la forma bactericida — a pH 7.2, aproximadamente el 67% del cloro libre está en esta forma efectiva. El cloro libre se consume por la luz UV, los contaminantes orgánicos y el propio acto de sanitización. Debe reponerse regularmente.
es.whyItMatters: Un cloro libre insuficiente permite que se establezcan bacterias y algas. Un exceso de cloro libre irrita a los bañistas. Ambos extremos se pueden evitar con análisis regulares.
es.typicalValues: Piscinas: 1–3 ppm; Hot tubs: 3–5 ppm; Mínimo seguro: 1.0 ppm

terms.definition: Free chlorine is the concentration of active, unsaturated chlorine available in pool water to sanitise and disinfect.
terms.explanation: Free chlorine consists of two forms: hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and hypochlorite ion (OCl-). Hypochlorous acid is the bactericidal form — at pH 7.2, roughly 67% of free chlorine is in this effective form. Free chlorine is consumed by UV light, organic contaminants, and the act of sanitisation itself. It must be replenished regularly.
terms.whyItMatters: Inadequate free chlorine allows bacteria and algae to establish. Excess free chlorine irritates swimmers. Both extremes are avoidable with regular testing.
terms.typicalValues: Pools: 1–3 ppm; Hot tubs: 3–5 ppm; Minimum safe: 1.0 ppm

es.definition: El cloro combinado es la parte del cloro total que ha reaccionado con compuestos de nitrógeno y ya no es un sanitizante eficaz.
es.explanation: El cloro combinado está formado principalmente por cloraminas — compuestos que se forman cuando el cloro libre reacciona con el amoníaco y el nitrógeno orgánico de los bañistas. Las cloraminas son de 40 a 80 veces más débiles que el cloro libre como desinfectantes. También son la principal causa del olor característico de la piscina y de la irritación ocular, a menudo atribuidos erróneamente a un exceso de cloro.
es.whyItMatters: Un cloro combinado por encima de 0.5 ppm indica la necesidad de un tratamiento de choque. Señala que el cloro libre se está agotando más rápido de lo que puede sanitizar.
es.typicalValues: Objetivo: 0 ppm; Umbral de acción: 0.5 ppm; Se calcula como: Cloro Total menos Cloro Libre

terms.definition: Combined chlorine is the portion of total chlorine that has reacted with nitrogen compounds and is no longer an effective sanitiser.
terms.explanation: Combined chlorine consists primarily of chloramines — compounds formed when free chlorine reacts with ammonia and organic nitrogen from bathers. Chloramines are 40–80 times weaker than free chlorine as disinfectants. They are also the primary cause of the characteristic pool smell and eye irritation often mistakenly attributed to too much chlorine.
terms.whyItMatters: Combined chlorine above 0.5 ppm indicates a need for shock treatment. It signals that free chlorine is being depleted faster than it can sanitise.
terms.typicalValues: Target: 0 ppm; Action threshold: 0.5 ppm; Calculated as: Total Chlorine minus Free Chlorine

es.definition: El cloro total es la suma del cloro libre y el cloro combinado en el agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: El cloro total se mide con pruebas DPD-3 o pruebas OTO. Indica la cantidad total de compuestos relacionados con el cloro en el agua, pero no distingue entre el sanitizante activo (cloro libre) y los subproductos inactivos (cloro combinado). Cuando el cloro libre es igual al cloro total, no hay cloro combinado en el agua.
es.whyItMatters: El cloro total por sí solo no es una cifra útil para la gestión — necesita el cloro libre y el cloro combinado por separado. Sin embargo, el cloro combinado solo puede calcularse si se tienen ambas lecturas, libre y total.
es.typicalValues: Debe ser igual o muy cercano al Cloro Libre (FC) en agua bien mantenida

terms.definition: Total chlorine is the sum of free chlorine and combined chlorine in pool water.
terms.explanation: Total chlorine is measured by DPD-3 tests or OTO tests. It tells you the full amount of chlorine-related compounds in the water but does not distinguish between the active sanitiser (free chlorine) and the inactive by-products (combined chlorine). When free chlorine equals total chlorine, there is no combined chlorine in the water.
terms.whyItMatters: Total chlorine alone is not a useful management number — you need free chlorine and combined chlorine separately. However, combined chlorine can only be calculated if you have both free and total chlorine readings.
terms.typicalValues: Should equal or closely approximate Free Chlorine (FC) in well-maintained water

es.definition: La cloración de ruptura es el proceso de agregar suficiente cloro libre para destruir todo el cloro combinado (cloraminas) en el agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: El punto de ruptura ocurre cuando se agrega cloro libre en aproximadamente 10 veces el nivel de cloro combinado. Por debajo del punto de ruptura, agregar cloro aumenta temporalmente el cloro combinado antes de destruirlo. En el punto de ruptura y más allá, las cloraminas se destruyen químicamente y el cloro libre sube bruscamente. Por eso las dosis de choque parciales pueden empeorar el problema de cloraminas antes de finalmente mejorarlo.
es.whyItMatters: La cloración de ruptura es la única forma confiable de eliminar las cloraminas del agua de la piscina. Sin ella, el cloro combinado se acumula, causando olor persistente, irritación y una sanitización reducida.
es.typicalValues: Dosis requerida: 10 veces la lectura de cloro combinado en ppm

terms.definition: Breakpoint chlorination is the process of adding enough free chlorine to destroy all combined chlorine (chloramines) in pool water.
terms.explanation: The breakpoint occurs when free chlorine is added at approximately 10 times the combined chlorine level. Below the breakpoint, adding chlorine temporarily increases combined chlorine before destroying it. At and beyond the breakpoint, chloramines are chemically destroyed and free chlorine rises sharply. This is why partial shock doses can worsen the chloramine problem before eventually improving it.
terms.whyItMatters: Breakpoint chlorination is the only reliable way to eliminate chloramines from pool water. Without it, combined chlorine accumulates, causing persistent odour, irritation, and reduced sanitation.
terms.typicalValues: Required dose: 10x the combined chlorine reading in ppm

es.definition: Un sanitizante es un agente químico que reduce la contaminación microbiana del agua de la piscina a niveles seguros para el contacto humano.
es.explanation: En aplicaciones de piscinas y spas, los sanitizantes principales son el cloro y el bromo. Los sanitizantes actúan oxidando y destruyendo las paredes celulares de bacterias, virus y algas al contacto. Los sanitizantes secundarios (UV, ozono) pueden reducir los niveles de cloro requeridos, pero no reemplazan el sanitizante residual que protege el agua entre tratamientos.
es.whyItMatters: Sin un sanitizante eficaz a un nivel adecuado, el agua de la piscina puede transmitir enfermedades relacionadas con el agua recreativa en cuestión de horas tras la contaminación.
es.typicalValues: Cloro: 1–3 ppm (piscinas); Bromo: 3–6 ppm

terms.definition: A sanitizer is a chemical agent that reduces microbial contamination in pool water to safe levels for human contact.
terms.explanation: In pool and spa applications, the primary sanitizers are chlorine and bromine. Sanitizers work by oxidising and destroying the cell walls of bacteria, viruses, and algae on contact. Secondary sanitizers (UV, ozone) can reduce the required chlorine levels but do not replace the residual sanitiser that protects water between treatments.
terms.whyItMatters: Without an effective sanitizer at an adequate level, pool water can transmit recreational water illnesses (RWIs) within hours of contamination.
terms.typicalValues: Chlorine: 1–3 ppm (pools); Bromine: 3–6 ppm

es.definition: Un oxidante es un producto químico que destruye contaminantes orgánicos en el agua de la piscina mediante oxidación, sin necesariamente agregar sanitizante residual.
es.explanation: El monopersulfato de potasio (MPS, choque sin cloro) es un oxidante común en piscinas. Destruye compuestos orgánicos como aceites corporales, sudor y precursores de cloraminas sin elevar el cloro libre. El cloro mismo es tanto sanitizante como oxidante. Los oxidantes se usan en hot tubs después de cada uso y en piscinas para complementar el choque semanal.
es.whyItMatters: La oxidación regular evita la acumulación orgánica que de otro modo agotaría el cloro y contribuiría a la formación de cloraminas.
es.typicalValues: MPS (choque sin cloro): siga la dosis indicada en la etiqueta del producto

terms.definition: An oxidizer is a chemical that destroys organic contaminants in pool water through oxidation, without necessarily adding sanitiser residual.
terms.explanation: Potassium monopersulfate (MPS, non-chlorine shock) is a common pool oxidizer. It destroys organic compounds like body oils, sweat, and chloramine precursors without raising free chlorine. Chlorine itself is both a sanitizer and an oxidizer. Oxidizers are used in hot tubs after each soak session to destroy organic load and in pools to supplement weekly shock treatment.
terms.whyItMatters: Regular oxidation prevents organic accumulation that would otherwise deplete chlorine and contribute to chloramine formation.
terms.typicalValues: MPS (non-chlorine shock): follow product label dosing

es.definition: El choque es la práctica de agregar una dosis grande de cloro u oxidante al agua de la piscina para alcanzar la cloración de ruptura, eliminar algas o restablecer la claridad del agua.
es.explanation: Los productos de choque para piscina suelen ser hipoclorito de calcio (65–73% de cloro disponible), dicloroisocianurato de sodio (dicloro) o hipoclorito de sodio en alta concentración. El choque eleva el cloro libre a 10 ppm o más — muy por encima del rango normal de mantenimiento. El choque sin cloro (MPS) se usa específicamente para oxidar materia orgánica sin elevar el cloro libre.
es.whyItMatters: El choque semanal es una práctica de mantenimiento preventivo que destruye las cloraminas y oxida los contaminantes orgánicos antes de que se acumulen a niveles problemáticos.
es.typicalValues: Objetivo de choque estándar: 10 ppm de FC; Recuperación de piscina verde: 30 ppm de FC

terms.definition: Shock is the practice of adding a large dose of chlorine or oxidizer to pool water to reach breakpoint chlorination, kill algae, or reset water clarity.
terms.explanation: Pool shock products are typically calcium hypochlorite (65–73% available chlorine), sodium dichloro-isocyanurate (dichlor), or sodium hypochlorite at high concentration. Shocking raises free chlorine to 10 ppm or higher — far above the normal maintenance range. Non-chlorine shock (MPS) is used specifically to oxidise organic material without raising free chlorine.
terms.whyItMatters: Weekly shocking is a preventive maintenance practice that destroys chloramines and oxidises organic contaminants before they accumulate to problem levels.
terms.typicalValues: Standard shock target: 10 ppm FC; Green pool recovery: 30 ppm FC

es.definition: El pH mide la concentración de iones de hidrógeno en el agua en una escala logarítmica de 0 (más ácido) a 14 (más alcalino), siendo 7.0 el valor neutro.
es.explanation: El pH del agua de la piscina controla directamente la proporción de cloro en su forma activa (ácido hipocloroso). A pH 7.2, aproximadamente el 67% del cloro libre está activo. A pH 8.0, solo el 22% lo está. El pH también afecta la comodidad de los bañistas (las lágrimas humanas tienen un pH de 7.4), la corrosión de superficies (pH bajo) y la formación de incrustaciones (pH alto). El pH tiende a subir naturalmente en las piscinas a medida que el CO2 se libera desde la superficie del agua.
es.whyItMatters: Todos los demás parámetros de la química del agua se ven afectados por el pH. Es la variable de control maestra en la gestión de la piscina.
es.typicalValues: Piscinas: 7.2–7.6; Hot tubs: 7.2–7.8; Nunca por encima de 8.0

terms.definition: pH measures the concentration of hydrogen ions in water on a logarithmic scale from 0 (most acidic) to 14 (most alkaline), with 7.0 being neutral.
terms.explanation: Pool water pH directly controls the proportion of chlorine in its active form (hypochlorous acid). At pH 7.2, approximately 67% of free chlorine is active. At pH 8.0, only 22% is active. pH also affects swimmer comfort (human tears are pH 7.4), surface corrosion (low pH), and scaling (high pH). pH naturally drifts upward in pools as CO2 off-gasses from the water surface.
terms.whyItMatters: Every other water chemistry parameter is affected by pH. It is the master control variable in pool management.
terms.typicalValues: Pools: 7.2–7.6; Hot tubs: 7.2–7.8; Never above 8.0

es.definition: La alcalinidad total mide la capacidad del agua para resistir cambios de pH, expresada como la concentración total de compuestos alcalinos (bicarbonato, carbonato, hidróxido) en ppm.
es.explanation: La alcalinidad total actúa como amortiguador de pH. Cuando la TA está en rango (80–120 ppm), el pH cambia lentamente después de adiciones químicas o factores ambientales. Cuando la TA es demasiado baja (por debajo de 60 ppm), el pH oscila de forma impredecible — una condición llamada rebote de pH. Cuando la TA es demasiado alta (por encima de 200 ppm), el pH se estanca cerca de 8.0 y es muy difícil de bajar.
es.whyItMatters: La alcalinidad es la base de una gestión estable del pH. Corrija primero la alcalinidad, y los ajustes de pH se vuelven mucho más predecibles y duraderos.
es.typicalValues: Piscinas y hot tubs: 80–120 ppm; Por debajo de 60 ppm: tome acción; Por encima de 200 ppm: reduzca

terms.definition: Total alkalinity measures the water's ability to resist changes in pH, expressed as the total concentration of alkaline compounds (bicarbonate, carbonate, hydroxide) in ppm.
terms.explanation: Total alkalinity acts as a pH buffer. When TA is in range (80–120 ppm), pH changes slowly after chemical additions or environmental inputs. When TA is too low (below 60 ppm), pH swings unpredictably — a condition called pH bounce. When TA is too high (above 200 ppm), pH locks near 8.0 and is very difficult to lower.
terms.whyItMatters: Alkalinity is the foundation of stable pH management. Fix alkalinity first, and pH adjustments become far more predictable and lasting.
terms.typicalValues: Pools and hot tubs: 80–120 ppm; Below 60 ppm: take action; Above 200 ppm: reduce

es.definition: La dureza cálcica mide la concentración de iones de calcio disueltos en el agua de la piscina, expresada en ppm.
es.explanation: La dureza cálcica determina si el agua es agresiva (subsaturada, disolverá calcio de las superficies) o incrustante (sobresaturada, depositará carbonato de calcio). Junto con el pH, la temperatura y la alcalinidad, determina el Índice de Saturación de Langelier. Las piscinas de yeso requieren una dureza más alta (200–400 ppm) para proteger las superficies. El vinilo y la fibra de vidrio toleran niveles más bajos (150–250 ppm).
es.whyItMatters: Una dureza baja corroe las superficies de yeso y el equipo. Una dureza alta deposita incrustaciones de calcio en calentadores, tuberías y azulejos.
es.typicalValues: Piscinas de yeso: 200–400 ppm; Vinilo/fibra de vidrio: 150–250 ppm; Hot tubs: 150–250 ppm

terms.definition: Calcium hardness measures the concentration of dissolved calcium ions in pool water, expressed in ppm.
terms.explanation: Calcium hardness determines whether water is aggressive (under-saturated, will dissolve calcium from surfaces) or scaling (over-saturated, will deposit calcium carbonate). Along with pH, temperature, and alkalinity, it determines the Langelier Saturation Index. Plaster pools require higher hardness (200–400 ppm) to protect surfaces. Vinyl and fibreglass tolerate lower levels (150–250 ppm).
terms.whyItMatters: Low hardness corrodes plaster surfaces and equipment. High hardness deposits calcium scale on heaters, pipes, and tile.
terms.typicalValues: Plaster pools: 200–400 ppm; Vinyl/fibreglass: 150–250 ppm; Hot tubs: 150–250 ppm

es.definition: El ácido cianúrico es un compuesto estabilizador que forma un enlace reversible con el cloro libre en el agua de la piscina, protegiéndolo de la degradación por rayos UV.
es.explanation: Sin CYA, el cloro libre de una piscina al aire libre se destruye por la luz solar directa en 2 a 3 horas. El CYA forma un enlace temporal con las moléculas de cloro, ralentizando su degradación por UV. Sin embargo, el CYA también reduce moderadamente la velocidad de sanitización del cloro. Por encima de 80 ppm, el efecto se vuelve lo suficientemente significativo como para que las dosis normales de cloro brinden una sanitización inadecuada.
es.whyItMatters: El CYA es esencial para piscinas al aire libre que usan cloro, pero debe mantenerse por debajo de 80 ppm. No se puede reducir salvo por dilución (drenaje parcial).
es.typicalValues: Piscinas estándar: 30–50 ppm; Piscinas salinas: 60–80 ppm; Nunca por encima de 100 ppm en piscinas normales

terms.definition: Cyanuric acid is a stabilizing compound that forms a reversible bond with free chlorine in pool water, protecting it from UV degradation.
terms.explanation: Without CYA, free chlorine in an outdoor pool is destroyed by direct sunlight within 2–3 hours. CYA forms a temporary bond with chlorine molecules, slowing UV breakdown. However, CYA also moderately reduces chlorine's sanitising speed. Above 80 ppm, the effect becomes significant enough that normal chlorine doses provide inadequate sanitisation.
terms.whyItMatters: CYA is essential for outdoor pools using chlorine, but must be kept below 80 ppm. It cannot be reduced except by dilution (partial drain).
terms.typicalValues: Standard pools: 30–50 ppm; Salt pools: 60–80 ppm; Never above 100 ppm for normal pools

es.definition: El Índice de Saturación de Langelier es un valor calculado que predice si el agua de la piscina está en equilibrio con el carbonato de calcio, tiende a corroer o tiende a formar incrustaciones.
es.explanation: LSI = pH + Factor de Temperatura + Factor de Calcio + Factor de Alcalinidad − 12.1. Un resultado de 0.0 es el balance perfecto. Los valores negativos indican agua agresiva (corrosiva); los valores positivos indican tendencia a formar incrustaciones. El rango objetivo es de −0.3 a +0.3. La temperatura es un factor importante — la misma química produce un LSI más alto a 90°F que a 70°F.
es.whyItMatters: El LSI es el indicador más completo del balance del agua. Tiene en cuenta todas las variables principales y predice tanto el daño al equipo (corrosión) como el daño a las superficies (incrustaciones).
es.typicalValues: Objetivo: −0.3 a +0.3; 0.0 = balance perfecto

terms.definition: The Langelier Saturation Index is a calculated number that predicts whether pool water is in equilibrium with calcium carbonate, tending to corrode, or tending to deposit scale.
terms.explanation: LSI = pH + Temperature Factor + Calcium Factor + Alkalinity Factor - 12.1. A result of 0.0 is perfect balance. Negative values indicate aggressive (corrosive) water; positive values indicate scaling tendency. The target range is -0.3 to +0.3. Temperature is a major factor — the same chemistry produces a higher LSI at 90°F than at 70°F.
terms.whyItMatters: The LSI is the most complete indicator of water balance. It accounts for all the major variables and predicts both equipment damage (corrosion) and surface damage (scaling).
terms.typicalValues: Target: -0.3 to +0.3; 0.0 = perfect balance

terms.definition: ORP is the electrical potential of water measured in millivolts that indicates the overall oxidising capacity of the water.
terms.explanation: ORP is measured with a probe and reflects the combined effect of free chlorine concentration and pH on the water's ability to oxidise contaminants. At an ORP above 650 mV, water is generally considered effective for sanitation. ORP is not a direct chlorine measurement — the same free chlorine reading produces very different ORP values at different pH levels. It is a useful supplemental indicator but does not replace direct chemical testing.
terms.whyItMatters: ORP probes provide a real-time, continuous indication of sanitiser activity without requiring reagent-based tests.
terms.typicalValues: Sanitation threshold: 650 mV; Optimal: 700–750 mV

terms.definition: Total dissolved solids measures the total concentration of all dissolved substances in pool water, expressed in ppm.
terms.explanation: TDS includes all dissolved salts, chemicals, minerals, and organic compounds. As pool water is used and chemicals are added, TDS increases. High TDS can reduce the effectiveness of sanitisers, interfere with water balance, and contribute to foam in hot tubs. The only way to lower TDS is to drain and replace a portion of the water.
terms.whyItMatters: TDS above 1,500 ppm over baseline (or above 3,000 ppm absolute) in a hot tub is a common trigger for water change. In pools, TDS is less critical but should be monitored.
terms.typicalValues: Hot tubs: change water when TDS exceeds 1,500 ppm over fill water baseline; Pools: monitor; Salt pools: 3,000–5,000 ppm (salt contributes significantly)

terms.definition: Filter pressure is the water pressure reading on the filter pressure gauge, measured in psi (pounds per square inch).
terms.explanation: When a filter is clean, it has a baseline pressure. As the filter captures particles and becomes partially clogged, pressure rises. The standard cleaning threshold is 8–10 psi above the clean baseline. An abnormally low pressure can indicate a pump problem or a disconnected filter. An abnormally high pressure indicates a clogged or partially blocked filter.
terms.whyItMatters: Filter pressure is the primary indicator of when the filter needs cleaning. Running a clogged filter reduces water flow and filtration efficiency.
terms.typicalValues: Baseline: varies by system; Clean threshold: baseline + 0–4 psi; Cleaning needed: baseline + 8–10 psi

terms.definition: Backwashing is the process of reversing water flow through a sand or DE filter to flush accumulated debris out of the filter media to waste.
terms.explanation: In a sand filter, backwashing is initiated by turning the multiport valve to the backwash position, which reverses water flow through the filter, dislodging and flushing captured particles out through a waste line. The backwash cycle continues until the sight glass (if present) runs clear, typically 2–3 minutes. After backwashing, run the filter on the rinse setting for 30 seconds before returning to normal operation.
terms.whyItMatters: Backwashing restores filter flow rate and filtration efficiency. Delaying backwashing beyond the 8–10 psi threshold reduces water quality.
terms.typicalValues: Backwash when filter pressure is 8–10 psi above clean baseline

es.definition: La recirculación de la bomba es la cantidad de veces que todo el volumen de la piscina pasa por el filtro en un período de 24 horas.
es.explanation: Una recirculación significa que todo el volumen de la piscina se ha filtrado una vez. El estándar mínimo de la industria es una recirculación cada 8 horas (3 recirculaciones por día). Más recirculaciones significan mejor filtración y distribución química. Las bombas de velocidad variable pueden lograr más recirculaciones al día con un menor costo energético, funcionando a velocidades más bajas durante períodos más largos.
es.whyItMatters: Una tasa de recirculación insuficiente es una de las causas más comunes de agua turbia persistente y problemas de algas, sin importar que la química sea correcta.
es.typicalValues: Mínimo: 1 recirculación cada 8 horas; Recomendado: 1–2 recirculaciones por día; Piscinas comerciales: a menudo 4–6 recirculaciones por día

terms.definition: Pump turnover is the number of times the entire pool volume passes through the filter in a 24-hour period.
terms.explanation: One turnover means the entire pool volume has been filtered once. The industry standard minimum is one turnover per 8 hours (3 turnovers per day). More turnovers mean better filtration and chemical distribution. Variable speed pumps can achieve more turnovers per day at lower energy cost by running at lower speeds for longer periods.
terms.whyItMatters: Insufficient turnover rate is one of the most common causes of persistent cloudy water and algae problems, regardless of correct chemistry.
terms.typicalValues: Minimum: 1 turnover per 8 hours; Recommended: 1–2 turnovers per day; Commercial pools: often 4–6 turnovers per day

terms.definition: A skimmer is a pool fitting built into the pool wall at the water surface that draws in surface water and floating debris for filtration.
terms.explanation: Pool skimmers use pump suction to draw surface water (and everything floating on it) into a basket-equipped housing where debris is captured before the water continues to the pump and filter. Correct water level is critical — the surface should be at the midpoint of the skimmer opening. Too low and the pump draws air; too high and the skimmer does not capture surface debris effectively.
terms.whyItMatters: Skimmers are the primary defence against surface debris that would otherwise sink, decompose, and contribute to chlorine demand and cloudiness.
terms.typicalValues: Water level at mid-skimmer opening; Empty basket every 2–3 days

terms.definition: A cartridge filter is a pool filter type that uses a pleated polyester element to capture particles as water passes from outside to inside the element.
terms.explanation: Cartridge filters capture particles down to 10–15 microns — finer than sand filters (20–40 microns). They require no backwashing (saving water) but need regular rinsing and periodic degreaser soaking. Cartridges are replaced annually or when they no longer return to baseline pressure after cleaning.
terms.whyItMatters: Cartridge filters produce clearer water than sand filters and are especially appropriate in water-restricted areas since they require no backwash water.
terms.typicalValues: Filtration fineness: 10–15 microns; Clean when pressure rises 8–10 psi above baseline

terms.definition: A sand filter is a pool filter type that passes water through a bed of specially graded silica sand to capture particles.
terms.explanation: Sand filters capture particles 20–40 microns and larger. Cleaning is done by backwashing — reversing water flow to flush debris to waste. Sand needs replacement every 5–7 years as the grains wear smooth and lose filtration effectiveness. Sand filters are durable, widely used, and require less frequent maintenance than cartridge filters, though they use water for backwashing.
terms.whyItMatters: Sand filters are the most common pool filter type. Understanding their maintenance needs (backwash threshold, sand replacement schedule) is essential for maintaining water quality.
terms.typicalValues: Filtration fineness: 20–40 microns; Backwash when pressure is 8–10 psi over baseline

es.definition: La supercloración es la práctica de elevar el cloro libre a 10 ppm o más para destruir cloraminas, eliminar algas o recuperar agua gravemente comprometida.
es.explanation: La supercloración y la cloración de ruptura están estrechamente relacionadas — ambas implican agregar suficiente cloro para destruir el cloro combinado. La supercloración a veces se usa como un término más amplio para cualquier tratamiento de cloro en dosis alta. Después de la supercloración, la piscina debe cerrarse a los bañistas hasta que el cloro libre baje de 5 ppm, típicamente en 24 horas con la bomba en funcionamiento.
es.whyItMatters: La supercloración es una de las herramientas más eficaces para recuperar una piscina de algas, turbidez o cloro combinado alto.
es.typicalValues: FC objetivo: 10 ppm (mínimo); Piscina verde: 30 ppm

terms.definition: Superchlorination is the practice of raising free chlorine to 10 ppm or higher to destroy chloramines, kill algae, or clear severely compromised water.
terms.explanation: Superchlorination and breakpoint chlorination are closely related — both involve adding enough chlorine to destroy combined chlorine. Superchlorination is sometimes used as a broader term for any high-dose chlorine treatment. After superchlorination, the pool must be closed to swimmers until FC drops below 5 ppm, typically within 24 hours with the pump running.
terms.whyItMatters: Superchlorination is one of the most effective tools for pool recovery from algae, cloudiness, or high combined chlorine.
terms.typicalValues: Target FC: 10 ppm (minimum); Green pool: 30 ppm

es.definition: Las cloraminas son compuestos que se forman cuando el cloro libre reacciona con compuestos nitrogenados en el agua de la piscina. Son la principal causa del olor de la piscina y la irritación ocular.
es.explanation: Las principales cloraminas en el agua de la piscina son la monocloramina (NH2Cl), la dicloramina (NHCl2) y el tricloruro de nitrógeno (NCl3). La monocloramina es relativamente leve. La dicloramina y el tricloruro de nitrógeno son volátiles y muy irritantes. Todas las cloraminas son desinfectantes mucho menos eficaces que el cloro libre. El cloro combinado es la suma de todas las especies de cloraminas en el agua de la piscina.
es.whyItMatters: Las cloraminas son la causa directa de los síntomas que la mayoría de las personas atribuyen a un exceso de cloro: ojos rojos, irritación de la piel y un fuerte olor químico.
es.typicalValues: Umbral de acción: 0.5 ppm de cloro combinado

terms.definition: Chloramines are compounds formed when free chlorine reacts with nitrogen-containing compounds in pool water. They are the primary cause of pool odour and eye irritation.
terms.explanation: The main chloramines in pool water are monochloramine (NH2Cl), dichloramine (NHCl2), and nitrogen trichloride (NCl3). Monochloramine is relatively mild. Dichloramine and nitrogen trichloride are volatile and highly irritating. All chloramines are far less effective disinfectants than free chlorine. Combined chlorine = the sum of all chloramine species in pool water.
terms.whyItMatters: Chloramines are the direct cause of the symptoms most people attribute to too much chlorine: red eyes, skin irritation, and strong chemical odour.
terms.typicalValues: Action threshold: 0.5 ppm combined chlorine

es.definition: El dicloro (dicloroisocianurato de sodio) es un producto de cloro estabilizado de disolución rápida que agrega tanto cloro libre como ácido cianúrico al agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: El dicloro contiene aproximadamente 56% de cloro disponible y cerca de 33% de CYA por peso. Se disuelve muy rápido — más rápido que el tricloro — lo que lo hace útil para aumentos rápidos de FC. Sin embargo, cada libra de dicloro agrega una cantidad significativa de CYA. El uso repetido como sanitizante principal o producto de choque lleva a la acumulación de CYA. El dicloro se usa mejor con moderación para aumentos rápidos de cloro, en lugar de como producto principal o de choque.
es.whyItMatters: Muchos propietarios de piscinas usan choque de dicloro repetidamente sin analizar el CYA, lo que lleva a una acumulación que eventualmente hace que la piscina no pueda sanitizarse.
es.typicalValues: Cloro disponible: ~56%; CYA agregado: ~33% del peso del producto

terms.definition: Dichlor (sodium dichloroisocyanurate) is a fast-dissolving stabilised chlorine product that adds both free chlorine and cyanuric acid to pool water.
terms.explanation: Dichlor contains approximately 56% available chlorine and about 33% CYA by weight. It dissolves very quickly — faster than trichlor — making it useful for quick FC increases. However, every pound of dichlor adds a significant amount of CYA. Repeated use as a primary sanitiser or shock product leads to CYA accumulation. Dichlor is best used sparingly for quick chlorine boosts rather than as a primary or shock product.
terms.whyItMatters: Many pool owners use dichlor shock repeatedly without testing CYA, leading to CYA accumulation that eventually makes the pool unsanitisable.
terms.typicalValues: Available chlorine: ~56%; CYA added: ~33% by weight of product

es.definition: El tricloro (ácido tricloroisocianúrico) es una tableta de cloro estabilizado de disolución lenta que entrega cloro libre y ácido cianúrico simultáneamente.
es.explanation: Las tabletas de tricloro contienen aproximadamente 90% de cloro disponible y son fuertemente ácidas (pH ~2.8 en solución). Cada tableta agrega CYA a medida que se disuelve. Usado como sanitizante principal, el tricloro es muy conveniente pero lleva a una acumulación de CYA durante la temporada. También baja el pH, requiriendo correcciones de pH más frecuentes. El tricloro no es adecuado como producto de choque porque la adición de CYA hace poco práctico aplicar tratamientos de dosis alta.
es.whyItMatters: El tricloro es el producto sanitizante para piscinas más utilizado, pero su aporte de CYA suele monitorearse poco, lo que provoca el problema de gestión de piscinas a largo plazo más común.
es.typicalValues: Cloro disponible: ~90%; CYA: ~58% por peso; pH en solución: ~2.8

terms.definition: Trichlor (trichloroisocyanuric acid) is a slow-dissolving stabilised chlorine tablet that delivers free chlorine and cyanuric acid simultaneously.
terms.explanation: Trichlor tablets contain approximately 90% available chlorine and are strongly acidic (pH ~2.8 in solution). Each tablet adds CYA as it dissolves. Used as the primary sanitiser, trichlor is very convenient but leads to CYA accumulation over a season. It also lowers pH, requiring more frequent pH correction. Trichlor is not suitable for use as a shock product because the CYA addition makes high-dose treatments impractical.
terms.whyItMatters: Trichlor is the most widely used pool sanitiser product, but its CYA contribution is chronically under-monitored, leading to the most common long-term pool management problem.
terms.typicalValues: Available chlorine: ~90%; CYA: ~58% by weight; pH in solution: ~2.8

es.definition: El hipoclorito de calcio es un compuesto de cloro granular usado principalmente como choque para piscina, con aproximadamente 65–73% de cloro disponible.
es.explanation: El cal-hipo es el producto de choque granular estándar para piscinas. Se disuelve por completo y agrega calcio al agua (relevante en zonas con dureza ya alta). No agrega CYA, lo que lo hace ideal para la cloración de ruptura y el choque regular. Predisuélvalo en un balde de agua antes de agregarlo a la piscina — nunca lo agregue directamente en el skimmer, ya que puede corroer el equipo.
es.whyItMatters: El cal-hipo es el producto de choque más eficaz y económico para el mantenimiento regular de la piscina. Comprender su aporte de calcio ayuda a prevenir incrustaciones en zonas con agua dura.
es.typicalValues: Cloro disponible: 65–73%; No agrega CYA; Agrega calcio

terms.definition: Calcium hypochlorite is a granular chlorine compound used primarily as pool shock, with approximately 65–73% available chlorine.
terms.explanation: Cal-hypo is the standard granular shock product for pools. It dissolves completely and adds calcium to the water (relevant in areas with already-high hardness). It does not add CYA, making it ideal for breakpoint chlorination and regular shocking. Pre-dissolve in a bucket of water before adding to the pool — never add directly to the skimmer, as it can corrode equipment.
terms.whyItMatters: Cal-hypo is the most effective and economical shock product for regular pool maintenance. Understanding its calcium contribution helps prevent scaling in hard-water areas.
terms.typicalValues: Available chlorine: 65–73%; Does not add CYA; Adds calcium

es.definition: El hipoclorito de sodio es cloro líquido — una solución de iones de sodio e hipoclorito usada para sanitizar y aplicar choque al agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: El hipoclorito de sodio de grado piscina se vende típicamente a una concentración de 10–12.5%. Sube el pH ligeramente con cada adición y no agrega CYA. Se degrada con el tiempo, perdiendo potencia después de 60 días de almacenamiento. El cloro líquido es el producto preferido para la sanitización regular cuando el CYA ya está en el rango objetivo, y para el tratamiento de choque porque no está estabilizado.
es.whyItMatters: El cloro líquido es el sanitizante profesional más común para piscinas. Comprender su degradación ayuda a evitar errores de dosificación por producto vencido.
es.typicalValues: Concentración: 10–12.5% (grado piscina); Vida útil: 60 días a temperatura ambiente

terms.definition: Sodium hypochlorite is liquid chlorine — a solution of sodium and hypochlorite ions used to sanitise and shock pool water.
terms.explanation: Pool-grade sodium hypochlorite is typically sold at 10–12.5% concentration. It raises pH slightly with each addition and does not add CYA. It degrades over time, losing potency after 60 days of storage. Liquid chlorine is the preferred product for regular sanitisation when CYA is already at target range, and for shock treatment because it is non-stabilised.
terms.whyItMatters: Liquid chlorine is the most common professional pool sanitiser. Understanding its degradation helps avoid dosing errors from old product.
terms.typicalValues: Concentration: 10–12.5% (pool grade); Shelf life: 60 days at room temperature

es.definition: El bromo es un sanitizante halógeno usado en el agua de piscinas y spas que forma ácido hipobromoso (HOBr) como su forma desinfectante activa.
es.explanation: El bromo funciona de manera similar al cloro, pero con diferencias clave: es más estable a altas temperaturas (preferido para hot tubs), se mantiene eficaz en un rango de pH más amplio (7.0–8.0), y el bromo consumido (bromuros) puede reactivarse agregando un oxidante. A diferencia del cloro, el bromo no puede estabilizarse contra los rayos UV, lo que lo hace poco práctico para piscinas al aire libre con luz solar directa. Objetivo de bromo: 3–6 ppm (en comparación con 1–3 ppm para el cloro).
es.whyItMatters: El bromo es el sanitizante preferido para spas y hot tubs de interior. Su estabilidad a altas temperaturas lo hace más eficaz que el cloro en estas aplicaciones.
es.typicalValues: Hot tubs y spas: 3–6 ppm; Piscinas de interior: 3–6 ppm

terms.definition: Bromine is a halogen sanitiser used in pool and spa water that forms hypobromous acid (HOBr) as its active disinfectant form.
terms.explanation: Bromine works similarly to chlorine but has key differences: it is more stable at high temperatures (preferred for hot tubs), it remains effective over a wider pH range (7.0–8.0), and spent bromine (bromides) can be reactivated by adding an oxidiser. Unlike chlorine, bromine cannot be stabilised against UV, making it impractical for outdoor pools in direct sunlight. Bromine target: 3–6 ppm (compared to 1–3 ppm for chlorine).
terms.whyItMatters: Bromine is the preferred sanitiser for indoor spas and hot tubs. Its stability at high temperatures makes it more effective than chlorine in these applications.
terms.typicalValues: Hot tubs and spas: 3–6 ppm; Indoor pools: 3–6 ppm

terms.definition: BCDMH (1-bromo-3-chloro-5,5-dimethylhydantoin) is the most common active ingredient in bromine tablets for hot tubs and spas.
terms.explanation: BCDMH tablets dissolve slowly to release bromine into spa water. They contain both bromine and chlorine in their molecular structure — the chlorine acts as the oxidiser to activate the bromine. BCDMH is the standard product for bromine floaters and automatic feeders in hot tubs. It is not suitable for outdoor pools where UV would rapidly destroy the bromine.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding BCDMH helps hot tub owners correctly interpret the product they are using and understand why bromine levels are more stable in indoor environments.
terms.typicalValues: Available bromine: ~54%; Dissolves in about 3–5 days (3-inch tablets)

es.definition: La cloración salina (generación de agua salada) es un sistema que produce cloro libre de forma continua mediante la electrólisis del cloruro de sodio disuelto en el agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: Los clorinadores salinos usan una célula salina de titanio para dividir las moléculas de cloruro de sodio con una corriente de bajo voltaje, produciendo ácido hipocloroso en la superficie de la célula. La piscina sigue usando la química del cloro — solo que lo genera a partir de sal en lugar de agregarlo manualmente. Las piscinas salinas todavía requieren gestión de pH, alcalinidad y dureza. Las células salinas forman incrustaciones de calcio y deben limpiarse cada 3 a 4 meses.
es.whyItMatters: La cloración salina reduce la necesidad de adiciones regulares de cloro, pero no elimina la gestión de la química del agua.
es.typicalValues: Nivel de sal: 2,700–3,400 ppm; CYA para piscinas salinas: 60–80 ppm

terms.definition: Salt chlorination (salt water generation) is a system that produces free chlorine continuously by electrolyzing dissolved sodium chloride in pool water.
terms.explanation: Salt chlorinators use a titanium salt cell to split sodium chloride molecules with a low-voltage DC current, producing hypochlorous acid at the cell surface. The pool still uses chlorine chemistry — it just generates it from salt rather than adding it manually. Salt pools still require pH, alkalinity, and hardness management. Salt cells scale with calcium deposits and need cleaning every 3–4 months.
terms.whyItMatters: Salt chlorination reduces the need for regular chlorine additions but does not eliminate water chemistry management.
terms.typicalValues: Salt level: 2,700–3,400 ppm; CYA for salt pools: 60–80 ppm

terms.definition: UV sanitization uses ultraviolet light to inactivate microorganisms in pool water as it passes through a UV chamber in the equipment line.
terms.explanation: UV sanitizers are installed inline in the return line. Water passes through a chamber exposed to UV-C light (254 nm), which disrupts the DNA of bacteria, viruses, and algae. UV is highly effective at inactivating Cryptosporidium, which is resistant to chlorine. UV systems do not provide a residual sanitiser — a chlorine or bromine residual is still required. UV reduces the amount of chlorine needed to maintain adequate residual.
terms.whyItMatters: UV systems can reduce chlorine demand by 50–80%, reducing chloramine formation and the quantity of chemicals needed.
terms.typicalValues: Requires a chlorine residual of 0.5–1.0 ppm minimum with UV supplementation

terms.definition: Ozone (O3) is a powerful oxidiser used in pool systems to reduce organic contamination, chlorine demand, and chloramine formation.
terms.explanation: Ozone generators produce O3 from air or oxygen and inject it into pool water. Ozone rapidly oxidises bacteria, viruses, and organic contaminants. However, ozone breaks down quickly in water and provides no residual protection. It must be combined with a chlorine or bromine residual. Ozone significantly reduces the chlorine demand and chloramine formation in heavily used pools.
terms.whyItMatters: Ozone can greatly reduce the chemical load on pool water, improving water feel and reducing chloramine odour in high-use commercial or residential pools.
terms.typicalValues: Reduces chlorine demand by 60–90%; Chlorine residual still required: 0.5–1.0 ppm minimum

es.definition: El ácido muriático (ácido clorhídrico diluido) es el producto químico más usado para bajar el pH y la alcalinidad total de la piscina.
es.explanation: El ácido muriático de grado piscina se vende a una concentración aproximada de 31.45% (20 Baumé). Es un ácido fuerte que debe manipularse con el equipo de protección adecuado (protección ocular, guantes resistentes a ácidos). Siempre agregue el ácido al agua (nunca el agua al ácido) para evitar salpicaduras. Después de agregar ácido muriático a la piscina, permita de 30 a 60 minutos de circulación de la bomba antes de volver a analizar el pH.
es.whyItMatters: El ácido muriático es el reductor de pH y de alcalinidad más económico y eficaz para piscinas.
es.typicalValues: Concentración: 31.45% (grado piscina); pH en solución: fuertemente ácido (0.1–0.5)

terms.definition: Muriatic acid (dilute hydrochloric acid) is the most commonly used chemical for lowering pool pH and total alkalinity.
terms.explanation: Pool-grade muriatic acid is sold at approximately 31.45% concentration (20 Baumé). It is a strong acid that must be handled with appropriate protective equipment (eye protection, acid-resistant gloves). Always add acid to water (not water to acid) to prevent spattering. After adding muriatic acid to the pool, allow 30–60 minutes of pump circulation before retesting pH.
terms.whyItMatters: Muriatic acid is the most economical and effective pH reducer and alkalinity reducer for pools.
terms.typicalValues: Concentration: 31.45% (pool grade); pH in solution: strongly acidic (0.1–0.5)

es.definition: El carbonato de sodio (carbonato de sosa) se usa para subir el pH del agua de la piscina con un efecto mínimo en la alcalinidad total.
es.explanation: El carbonato de sosa (Na2CO3) se disuelve rápidamente en el agua de la piscina y sube el pH más rápido que el bicarbonato de sodio. Su efecto principal es la elevación del pH; su aporte a la alcalinidad es menor que el del bicarbonato de sodio. Es el producto preferido cuando el pH necesita subir sin aumentar significativamente la TA. Disuélvalo en un balde de agua antes de agregarlo a la piscina para evitar la turbidez blanquecina que dejan los gránulos sin disolver.
es.whyItMatters: El carbonato de sodio es el producto estándar para subir el pH de la piscina sin sobrecorregir la alcalinidad.
es.typicalValues: Sube el pH aproximadamente 0.2 unidades por libra por cada 10,000 galones

terms.definition: Sodium carbonate (soda ash) is used to raise pool water pH with minimal effect on total alkalinity.
terms.explanation: Soda ash (Na2CO3) dissolves quickly in pool water and raises pH more quickly than sodium bicarbonate. Its primary effect is pH elevation; its alkalinity contribution is less than that of sodium bicarbonate. It is the preferred product when pH needs to be raised without significantly increasing TA. Dissolve in a bucket of water before adding to the pool to prevent white cloudiness from undissolved granules.
terms.whyItMatters: Sodium carbonate is the standard product for raising pool pH without over-correcting alkalinity.
terms.typicalValues: Raises pH by approximately 0.2 units per pound per 10,000 gallons

es.definition: El bicarbonato de sodio (bicarbonato) es el producto químico estándar para subir la alcalinidad total en el agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: El bicarbonato de sodio (NaHCO3) se disuelve lentamente en el agua de la piscina y sube principalmente la alcalinidad total, con un efecto modesto en el pH. Es el producto más seguro y práctico para aumentar la TA. Una libra sube la TA aproximadamente 6.7 ppm por cada 10,000 galones. Espárzalo por el perímetro de la piscina con la bomba en funcionamiento, espere de 4 a 6 horas y vuelva a analizar antes de agregar más.
es.whyItMatters: El bicarbonato de sodio es el primer ajuste químico en la secuencia correcta de balance del agua, ya que estabiliza el pH y hace que los ajustes posteriores sean más predecibles.
es.typicalValues: Sube la TA 6.7 ppm por libra por cada 10,000 galones; efecto mínimo en el pH

terms.definition: Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) is the standard chemical for raising total alkalinity in pool water.
terms.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) dissolves slowly in pool water and primarily raises total alkalinity with a modest effect on pH. It is the safest and most practical product for increasing TA. One pound raises TA by approximately 6.7 ppm per 10,000 gallons. Broadcast it around the pool perimeter with the pump running, allow 4–6 hours, and retest before adding more.
terms.whyItMatters: Sodium bicarbonate is the first chemical adjustment in the correct water balance sequence, as it stabilises pH and makes subsequent adjustments more predictable.
terms.typicalValues: Raises TA by 6.7 ppm per pound per 10,000 gallons; minimal pH effect

es.definition: El bisulfato de sodio (ácido seco) es un ácido granular usado para bajar el pH y la alcalinidad total de la piscina, como alternativa más segura al ácido muriático líquido.
es.explanation: El bisulfato de sodio se vende como Reductor de pH o Ácido Seco. Es menos peligroso de manipular que el ácido muriático y no produce vapores. Sin embargo, es más costoso por dosis efectiva. Al disolverse en agua, produce ácido sulfúrico, que tiene el mismo efecto en la química de la piscina que el ácido muriático. Predisuélvalo en un balde de agua antes de agregarlo a la piscina.
es.whyItMatters: El ácido seco es el reductor de pH preferido para aplicaciones donde manipular ácido líquido no es práctico o donde la seguridad del almacenamiento químico es una preocupación.
es.typicalValues: Pureza: 93.2% NaHSO4; Baja el pH de forma similar al ácido muriático, pero a un mayor costo por dosis efectiva

terms.definition: Sodium bisulfate (dry acid) is a granular acid used to lower pool pH and total alkalinity as a safer alternative to liquid muriatic acid.
terms.explanation: Sodium bisulfate is sold as pH Down or Dry Acid. It is less hazardous to handle than muriatic acid and does not produce fumes. However, it is more expensive per effective dose. When dissolved in water, it produces sulfuric acid, which has the same effect on pool chemistry as muriatic acid. Pre-dissolve in a bucket of water before adding to the pool.
terms.whyItMatters: Dry acid is the preferred pH reducer for applications where liquid acid handling is impractical or where chemical storage safety is a concern.
terms.typicalValues: Purity: 93.2% NaHSO4; Lowers pH similarly to muriatic acid but at higher cost per effective dose

es.definition: El rebote de pH es la condición en la que el pH del agua de la piscina oscila de forma rápida e impredecible, típicamente causada por una alcalinidad total insuficiente.
es.explanation: Cuando la alcalinidad total está por debajo de 60 ppm, la capacidad amortiguadora del agua es inadecuada. Pequeñas adiciones de ácido o base, la lluvia, o incluso la actividad de los bañistas, pueden hacer que el pH oscile entre 0.5 y 1.0 unidades. El síntoma es un pH que se corrigió ayer pero que hoy vuelve a estar fuera de rango. La solución siempre es subir primero la alcalinidad total a 80–120 ppm, lo que estabiliza el sistema amortiguador.
es.whyItMatters: El rebote de pH es frustrante y desperdicia producto. Comprender la causa raíz (alcalinidad baja) evita semanas de persecución infructuosa del pH.
es.typicalValues: Ocurre cuando la TA está por debajo de 60 ppm

terms.definition: pH bounce is the condition where pool water pH swings rapidly and unpredictably, typically caused by insufficient total alkalinity.
terms.explanation: When total alkalinity is below 60 ppm, the buffering capacity of the water is inadequate. Small additions of acid or base, rain, or even bather activity can cause pH to swing by 0.5–1.0 units. The symptom is a pH that was corrected yesterday but is out of range again today. The fix is always to raise total alkalinity to 80–120 ppm first, which stabilises the buffering system.
terms.whyItMatters: pH bounce is frustrating and wasteful. Understanding the root cause (low alkalinity) prevents weeks of fruitless pH chasing.
terms.typicalValues: Occurs when TA is below 60 ppm

es.definition: Estabilizador de cloro es otro nombre para el ácido cianúrico (CYA), usado como sinónimo especialmente en el marketing de productos.
es.explanation: Los términos estabilizador, acondicionador y ácido cianúrico se refieren todos al mismo compuesto (C3H3N3O3). Las etiquetas de los productos suelen usar el término comercial estabilizador en lugar del nombre químico. Cuando la etiqueta de un producto indica que contiene estabilizador, está agregando CYA al agua. Esta distinción importa al monitorear la acumulación de CYA, ya que tanto los productos estabilizadores explícitos como las tabletas de cloro estabilizado (tricloro, dicloro) contribuyen a los niveles de CYA.
es.whyItMatters: Reconocer que estabilizador y CYA son lo mismo evita la adición accidental excesiva de CYA proveniente de varias fuentes de producto.
es.typicalValues: Objetivo: 30–50 ppm (piscinas estándar); 60–80 ppm (piscinas salinas)

terms.definition: Chlorine stabilizer is another name for cyanuric acid (CYA), used as a synonym especially in product marketing.
terms.explanation: The terms stabilizer, conditioner, and cyanuric acid all refer to the same compound (C3H3N3O3). Product labels often use the marketing term stabilizer rather than the chemical name. When a product label says it contains stabilizer, it is adding CYA to the water. This distinction matters when tracking CYA accumulation, since both explicit stabilizer products and stabilised chlorine tablets (trichlor, dichlor) contribute to CYA levels.
terms.whyItMatters: Recognising that stabilizer and CYA are the same thing prevents accidental over-addition of CYA from multiple product sources.
terms.typicalValues: Target: 30–50 ppm (standard pools); 60–80 ppm (salt pools)

es.definition: El ácido hipocloroso (HOCl) es la forma activa y bactericida del cloro en el agua de la piscina, responsable de eliminar patógenos.
es.explanation: Cuando el cloro se disuelve en agua, forma tanto HOCl como OCl- (ion hipoclorito). El HOCl es aproximadamente 80 veces más eficaz como desinfectante que el OCl-. La proporción de HOCl está controlada completamente por el pH — a pH 7.2, cerca del 67% es HOCl; a pH 8.0, solo el 22% es HOCl. Por eso un pH alto reduce drásticamente la eficacia del cloro incluso cuando la lectura de cloro libre total es adecuada.
es.whyItMatters: Comprender el HOCl explica por qué la gestión del pH es inseparable de la gestión del cloro en las piscinas.

terms.definition: Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is the active, bactericidal form of chlorine in pool water, responsible for killing pathogens.
terms.explanation: When chlorine dissolves in water, it forms both HOCl and OCl- (hypochlorite ion). HOCl is approximately 80 times more effective as a disinfectant than OCl-. The proportion of HOCl is controlled entirely by pH — at pH 7.2, about 67% is HOCl; at pH 8.0, only 22% is HOCl. This is why high pH drastically reduces chlorine effectiveness even when the total FC reading is adequate.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding HOCl explains why pH management is inseparable from chlorine management in pools.
terms.typicalValues: At pH 7.2: ~67% of FC is HOCl; at pH 7.4: ~55%; at pH 7.6: ~40%; at pH 8.0: ~22%

es.definition: Un brote de algas es la multiplicación rápida y visible de algas en el agua de la piscina, que da como resultado agua verde, turbia o descolorida.
es.explanation: Los brotes de algas comienzan cuando el cloro libre cae por debajo del mínimo eficaz (a menudo por debajo de 1 ppm, o por debajo del mínimo ajustado por CYA en piscinas estabilizadas) durante más de 24 horas. El agua tibia, la luz solar y los nutrientes de los bañistas aceleran el desarrollo del brote. El alga verde es la más común. El alga negra es más resistente y se establece como una biopelícula en las superficies de la piscina.
es.whyItMatters: Los brotes de algas hacen que el agua no sea segura para nadar y requieren de 24 a 72 horas de tratamiento intensivo para eliminarse.
es.typicalValues: Dosis de choque para un brote activo: 30 ppm de FC; Prevención: mantenga el FC por encima de 1 ppm en todo momento

terms.definition: An algae bloom is the rapid, visible multiplication of algae in pool water, resulting in green, cloudy, or discolored water.
terms.explanation: Algae blooms begin when free chlorine drops below the effective minimum (often below 1 ppm, or below the CYA-adjusted minimum for stabilised pools) for more than 24 hours. Warm water, sunlight, and nutrients from bathers accelerate bloom development. Green algae is the most common. Black algae is more resistant and establishes as a biofilm on pool surfaces.
terms.whyItMatters: Algae blooms make water unsafe for swimming and require 24–72 hours of intensive treatment to clear.
terms.typicalValues: Shock dose for active bloom: 30 ppm FC; Prevention: maintain FC above 1 ppm at all times

es.definition: El alga verde es la especie de alga más común en piscinas, y hace que el agua se torne verde o azul verdosa y que las superficies se vuelvan resbaladizas.
es.explanation: El alga verde (Chlorophyta) flota libremente en el agua cuando comienza a brotar y se deposita en las superficies a medida que madura. Se elimina manteniendo un cloro libre adecuado, pero forma una biopelícula que debe cepillarse físicamente antes del tratamiento de choque para permitir que el cloro penetre. El alga verde se vuelve gris blanquecina al morir — esta materia muerta debe filtrarse o aspirarse.
es.whyItMatters: El alga verde es la emergencia de piscina más común. Conocer el protocolo de tratamiento correcto evita semanas de tratamiento ineficaz.
es.typicalValues: Dosis de eliminación: 30 ppm de FC (brote activo); Mantenga 1–3 ppm de FC para prevenir

terms.definition: Green algae is the most common pool algae species, causing water to turn green or teal and surfaces to become slippery.
terms.explanation: Green algae (Chlorophyta) is free-floating in the water when first blooming and deposits on surfaces as it matures. It is killed by maintaining adequate free chlorine but establishes a biofilm that must be physically brushed before shock treatment to allow the chlorine to penetrate. Green algae turns grey-white when killed — this dead matter must be filtered or vacuumed out.
terms.whyItMatters: Green algae is the most common pool emergency. Knowing the correct treatment protocol prevents weeks of ineffective treatment.
terms.typicalValues: Kill dose: 30 ppm FC (active bloom); Maintain 1–3 ppm FC to prevent

es.definition: El alga negra es una especie de alga persistente y profundamente arraigada que forma manchas negras o verde azuladas oscuras en las superficies de yeso de la piscina.
es.explanation: A pesar de su nombre, el alga negra es una cianobacteria y no un alga verdadera. Forma una capa protectora externa (vaina) que resiste los niveles normales de cloro. El tratamiento requiere cepillar físicamente las manchas con fuerza usando un cepillo de cerdas duras para romper la capa protectora, y luego mantener niveles de FC muy altos (20–30 ppm) durante varios días. El alga negra a menudo reaparece si no se trata por completo.
es.whyItMatters: El alga negra es la más difícil de eliminar de todas las algas de piscina y a menudo indica un déficit de cloro prolongado.
es.typicalValues: Tratamiento: 20–30 ppm de FC mantenido durante 3 a 5 días; requiere cepillado vigoroso

terms.definition: Black algae is a stubborn, deeply rooted algae species that forms black or dark blue-green spots on pool plaster surfaces.
terms.explanation: Despite its name, black algae is a cyanobacterium rather than a true algae. It establishes a protective outer layer (sheath) that resists normal chlorine levels. Treatment requires physically scrubbing the spots aggressively with a stiff brush to break the protective layer, then maintaining very high FC levels (20–30 ppm) for several days. Black algae often recurs if not fully treated.
terms.whyItMatters: Black algae is the hardest pool algae to eliminate and often indicates a long-standing chlorine deficit.
terms.typicalValues: Treatment: 20–30 ppm FC maintained for 3–5 days; requires vigorous brushing

es.definition: El alga mostaza es una especie de alga de color amarillo pardo en piscinas que se cepilla fácilmente pero regresa rápido, causada por una cepa resistente al cloro.
es.explanation: El alga mostaza (variantes de Phaeophyta) se deposita como una sustancia polvorienta de color amarillo o mostaza en las paredes y el piso de la piscina, particularmente en áreas sombreadas. Se cepilla con facilidad y puede confundirse con arena o polen. Sin embargo, reaparece en pocos días sin un tratamiento sostenido de cloro alto. Es resistente a los niveles normales de cloro, pero se trata eficazmente con una supercloración completa de 30 ppm de FC y el tratamiento simultáneo de todo el equipo que estuvo en contacto con el agua.
es.whyItMatters: El alga mostaza a menudo se confunde con suciedad o arena, lo que lleva a tratamientos repetidos e ineficaces. Reconocerla permite un tratamiento de choque específico.
es.typicalValues: Tratamiento: 30 ppm de FC; lave toda la ropa de baño y el equipo durante el tratamiento

terms.definition: Mustard algae is a yellow-brown pool algae species that brushes off easily but quickly returns, caused by a chlorine-resistant strain.
terms.explanation: Mustard algae (Phaeophyta variants) deposits as a powdery yellow or mustard-coloured substance on pool walls and floors, particularly in shaded areas. It brushes off easily and can be mistaken for sand or pollen. However, it re-establishes within days without a sustained high-chlorine treatment. It is resistant to normal chlorine levels but is effectively treated with a thorough superchlorination of 30 ppm FC and simultaneous treatment of all equipment that contacted the water.
terms.whyItMatters: Mustard algae is often misdiagnosed as dirt or sand, leading to repeated ineffective treatments. Recognising it allows targeted shock treatment.
terms.typicalValues: Treatment: 30 ppm FC; wash all swimwear and equipment during treatment

terms.definition: Biofilm is a protective matrix of bacteria and organic material that establishes on pool and spa plumbing surfaces.
terms.explanation: Biofilm forms when bacteria adhere to surfaces and produce a polysaccharide matrix that protects them from sanitisers. In pool and spa plumbing, biofilm colonises the inside of pipes, jets, and heater components. Biofilm is resistant to normal chlorine levels and requires periodic mechanical disruption (line flush products) or periodic high-dose treatments. Flushing the plumbing before a spa water change is the most effective routine treatment.
terms.whyItMatters: Biofilm is a persistent source of organic contamination that recontaminates fresh water almost immediately if not addressed during a water change.
terms.typicalValues: Address with pipe flush product before each hot tub drain and refill

terms.definition: An algaecide is a chemical product that prevents algae growth or assists in killing established algae in pool water.
terms.explanation: Pool algaecides are typically quaternary ammonium compounds (quats) or copper-based compounds. Quats are most common and act as a supplemental preventive treatment — they do not replace free chlorine as the primary algae control. Copper-based algaecides are effective but can cause blue-green staining in soft or aggressive water. Algaecides should be used as a weekly maintenance dose or after a shock treatment, not as an emergency treatment for an established bloom.
terms.whyItMatters: Algaecide is a useful maintenance supplement but is frequently misused as an emergency green pool treatment, where it is ineffective.
terms.typicalValues: Follow product label; typically 1–4 fl oz per 10,000 gallons weekly as maintenance

terms.definition: A pool clarifier is a coagulant product that causes fine suspended particles to clump together into larger particles that the filter can capture.
terms.explanation: Clarifiers contain polyelectrolyte compounds that cause fine particles (which would otherwise pass through the filter) to aggregate into larger clusters that the filter can capture. They work best when the filter is functioning correctly and pool chemistry is in balance. Using clarifier without correcting the underlying chemistry issue (typically low FC or high pH) will only temporarily improve clarity.
terms.whyItMatters: Clarifier is effective for polishing water after chemistry has been corrected but is ineffective as a standalone treatment.
terms.typicalValues: Follow product label; do not overdose — excess clarifier can clog the filter

terms.definition: A pool flocculant is a coagulating agent that causes all suspended particles to clump and sink to the pool floor for vacuuming to waste.
terms.explanation: Unlike clarifiers (which coagulate particles for filter capture), flocculants (floc) cause rapid, heavy aggregation that drops particles to the pool bottom as a heavy sediment. After adding floc and allowing particles to settle (typically 8–12 hours with the pump off), the settled debris is vacuumed to waste — bypassing the filter entirely. Floc produces faster, more dramatic clarity improvement than clarifier but requires the ability to vacuum to waste.
terms.whyItMatters: Flocculant is the fastest way to clear severely cloudy water but requires follow-up vacuuming and cannot be used if the pool cannot be vacuumed to waste.
terms.typicalValues: Follow product label; pump must be off during settling period

terms.definition: A metal sequestrant is a pool chemical that binds dissolved metals (iron, copper, manganese) to prevent them from staining pool surfaces.
terms.explanation: When dissolved metals are present in pool water (from source water, algaecide, or corroded equipment), shocking the pool can cause them to oxidise and precipitate as stains. Metal sequestrant products (phosphonate or EDTA-based) bind metal ions in solution, keeping them from depositing as stains. They must be added before shocking when metals are suspected. They do not remove metals — they keep them in solution until they can be reduced through dilution.
terms.whyItMatters: Adding shock to a pool with dissolved copper or iron without first adding a sequestrant is a common cause of blue-green or brown staining.
terms.typicalValues: Follow product label; add before shock when metals are suspected or confirmed

terms.definition: A scale inhibitor is a pool product that prevents calcium carbonate from precipitating onto pool surfaces, tile, and equipment.
terms.explanation: Scale inhibitors (typically phosphonate or polyacrylic acid compounds) interfere with calcium carbonate crystal formation, keeping calcium in solution at concentrations that would otherwise deposit scale. They are used in areas with hard water, in heated pools, and in salt pools where scaling tendency is high. Scale inhibitors are a management tool — they do not replace proper LSI management but provide an additional buffer.
terms.whyItMatters: Scale inhibitor prevents the expensive, time-consuming removal of calcium deposits from tile, heater elements, and salt cells.
terms.typicalValues: Follow product label; typically weekly addition

terms.definition: DPD (N,N-diethyl-p-phenylenediamine) is the standard reagent used in liquid test kits to measure free chlorine and total chlorine.
terms.explanation: DPD-1 reagent reacts with free chlorine only, producing a pink colour proportional to FC concentration. DPD-3 (or DPD-1 plus a second reagent) reacts with total chlorine. The difference between the two readings is combined chlorine. DPD tests are more accurate than OTO tests because they specifically measure free chlorine rather than total chlorine. Always compare DPD colour tubes in natural or bright white light.
terms.whyItMatters: DPD is the gold standard for free chlorine measurement. Using OTO tests instead gives total chlorine, which overstates effective sanitiser levels.
terms.typicalValues: DPD-1 measures free chlorine (FC); DPD-3 measures total chlorine (TC)

terms.definition: OTO (orthotolidine) is an older test reagent that measures total chlorine by producing a yellow colour in chlorinated water.
terms.explanation: OTO produces a yellow colour in the presence of any chlorine species — both free chlorine and combined chlorine. It cannot distinguish between active and inactive chlorine. Two-way test kits sold inexpensively often use OTO for chlorine testing. Using OTO creates the risk of assuming the water is adequately sanitised when it may have adequate total chlorine but very low free chlorine and high combined chlorine.
terms.whyItMatters: OTO tests are not recommended for accurate pool management because they cannot detect the difference between effective and ineffective chlorine.
terms.typicalValues: Measures total chlorine (combined + free); DPD is preferred

terms.definition: A test strip is a plastic strip with reagent-impregnated pads that produce colour changes when dipped in pool water, indicating chemical concentrations.
terms.explanation: Test strips are convenient for quick daily checks but less accurate than liquid DPD kits. They are affected by storage conditions, dip time, reading delay, and light conditions during colour comparison. For parameters where precision matters (CYA, combined chlorine), liquid kits should be used. Test strips are most useful for rapid daily FC and pH screening, with liquid kit verification monthly.
terms.whyItMatters: Test strips are the most widely used consumer testing method. Understanding their limitations helps users know when to cross-check with a liquid kit.
terms.typicalValues: Accuracy: ±10–20% in ideal conditions; worse in high humidity or with old strips

terms.definition: A reagent is a chemical used in a water test kit that reacts with the parameter being measured to produce a measurable colour change.
terms.explanation: Pool test kits contain multiple reagents, each targeting a specific water parameter. DPD-1 and DPD-3 reagents measure free and total chlorine. Phenol Red measures pH. Other reagents measure alkalinity, hardness, and CYA. Reagents have a shelf life (typically 2 years if stored correctly) and degrade when exposed to heat, humidity, light, or chemical vapour.
terms.whyItMatters: Degraded reagents produce incorrect readings. Replacing reagents annually is essential for reliable test results.
terms.typicalValues: Shelf life: 2 years from manufacture date; replace annually for regular users

es.definition: Partes por millón (ppm) es la unidad usada para expresar la concentración de sustancias disueltas en el agua de la piscina, equivalente a miligramos por litro (mg/L).
es.explanation: Un ppm equivale a un miligramo de sustancia por litro de agua, o una parte de sustancia por cada millón de partes de agua en peso. Para la gestión de piscinas, el ppm se usa para expresar el cloro, los efectos de los productos de ajuste de pH, la dureza cálcica, la alcalinidad, el CYA y las concentraciones de sal. Todas las lecturas de los kits de prueba y los rangos objetivo de la piscina se expresan en ppm.
es.whyItMatters: Comprender el ppm como unidad de medida es un requisito previo para interpretar todos los resultados de las pruebas de química de la piscina y los cálculos de dosis químicas.

terms.definition: Parts per million (ppm) is the unit used to express the concentration of dissolved substances in pool water, equivalent to milligrams per liter (mg/L).
terms.explanation: One ppm equals one milligram of substance per liter of water, or one part substance per one million parts of water by weight. For pool management, ppm is used to express chlorine, pH adjustment chemical effects, calcium hardness, alkalinity, CYA, and salt concentrations. All pool test kit readings and target ranges are expressed in ppm.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding ppm as a measurement unit is prerequisite for interpreting all pool chemistry test results and chemical dose calculations.

terms.definition: Turbidity is the cloudiness or haziness of pool water caused by suspended fine particles that scatter light.
terms.explanation: Pool water turbidity can be caused by fine particles, dead algae, calcium carbonate precipitation, oils, or inadequate filtration. A standard visual test is whether you can clearly see the main drain from the pool deck — if not, turbidity is unacceptably high. NTU (nephelometric turbidity units) is the technical measurement, but for pools, the visual drain test is the practical standard.
terms.whyItMatters: High turbidity is both a safety concern (obscures a drowning person from view) and a chemistry indicator (usually signals an underlying water quality problem).
terms.typicalValues: Target: visible main drain from pool deck; <1 NTU for public pools

terms.definition: Bather load refers to the number and duration of swimmers in a pool, which affects chlorine consumption and organic contamination levels.
terms.explanation: Every bather introduces organic nitrogen compounds (sweat, body oils, sunscreen, urine) into the water. These compounds consume free chlorine and generate combined chlorine. A heavy bather load — a pool party, vacation rental with multiple guests, or a commercial pool at peak hours — can consume the entire free chlorine residual within hours. Testing after any heavy bather load event and adding appropriate chlorine is essential.
terms.whyItMatters: Bather load is one of the most significant variables in chlorine demand and is the primary reason why a consistent maintenance schedule can fail on busy days.
terms.typicalValues: Residential pool: 3–6 bathers is low load; 10+ bathers is high load requiring post-event testing and likely shock

es.definition: La demanda de cloro es la cantidad total de cloro consumido por todas las reacciones en el agua de la piscina antes de que se pueda establecer un residual de cloro libre.
es.explanation: Cuando el agua de la piscina no tiene cloro libre, pero al agregar cloro no se produce un residual (el FC marca cero inmediatamente después de la dosis), el agua tiene una demanda de cloro alta. Esto puede ser causado por contaminación orgánica intensa, algas, cloro combinado alto o CYA muy alto. La demanda debe satisfacerse completamente antes de que persista un residual de cloro libre. Alcanzar la cloración de ruptura satisface la demanda causada por el cloro combinado.
es.whyItMatters: Comprender la demanda de cloro explica por qué agregar cloro a algunas piscinas parece no producir resultados — la demanda debe satisfacerse antes de que se acumule el residual.
es.typicalValues: La demanda se satisface por completo cuando la lectura de FC permanece estable entre 15 y 30 minutos después de la adición

terms.definition: Chlorine demand is the total amount of chlorine consumed by all reactions in pool water before a free chlorine residual can be established.
terms.explanation: When pool water has no free chlorine but the addition of chlorine does not produce a residual (FC reads zero immediately after dosing), the water has a high chlorine demand. This can be caused by heavy organic contamination, algae, high combined chlorine, or very high CYA. The demand must be fully satisfied before a free chlorine residual will persist. Reaching breakpoint chlorination satisfies the demand caused by combined chlorine.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding chlorine demand explains why adding chlorine to some pools seems to produce no results — the demand must be met before residual builds.
terms.typicalValues: Demand is fully satisfied when FC reading remains stable 15–30 minutes after addition

es.definition: El volumen de piscina es la capacidad total de una piscina en galones, usada como base para todos los cálculos de dosis químicas.
es.explanation: El volumen de la piscina se calcula a partir de sus dimensiones y forma. Para piscinas rectangulares: Largo × Ancho × Profundidad Promedio × 7.48. Para piscinas circulares: π × r² × Profundidad × 7.48. Los errores de volumen de incluso un 10% se traducen directamente en errores equivalentes en cada dosis química. Conocer el volumen exacto de la piscina es el requisito previo más importante para una gestión correcta.
es.whyItMatters: Cada cálculo de dosis química requiere el volumen de la piscina como dato de entrada. Una estimación incorrecta del volumen hace que todas las dosis químicas resulten proporcionalmente erróneas.
es.typicalValues: Piscinas residenciales: 8,000–40,000 galones; Hot tubs: 200–600 galones

terms.definition: Pool volume is the total capacity of a pool in gallons, used as the basis for all chemical dose calculations.
terms.explanation: Pool volume is calculated from the pool's dimensions and shape. For rectangular pools: Length × Width × Average Depth × 7.48. For circular pools: π × r² × Depth × 7.48. Volume errors of even 10% translate directly into equivalent errors in every chemical dose. Knowing the accurate pool volume is the single most important prerequisite for correct pool management.
terms.whyItMatters: Every chemical dose calculation requires pool volume as an input. An incorrect volume estimate causes all chemical doses to be proportionally wrong.
terms.typicalValues: Residential pools: 8,000–40,000 gallons; Hot tubs: 200–600 gallons

es.definition: Una bomba de piscina es el dispositivo mecánico que hace circular el agua a través del filtro, el calentador y el clorinador, manteniendo el movimiento del agua y la filtración.
es.explanation: Las bombas de piscina crean succión al girar un impulsor que extrae agua del skimmer y el drenaje principal, la empuja a través del filtro y otros equipos, y la devuelve a la piscina por los retornos. El dimensionamiento de la bomba debe coincidir con el volumen de la piscina y la resistencia de las tuberías para lograr una tasa de recirculación adecuada. Las bombas de velocidad variable pueden ajustar su velocidad para ahorrar energía mientras mantienen una circulación adecuada.
es.whyItMatters: La bomba es el corazón del sistema de la piscina. Sin una circulación adecuada, ningún tratamiento químico puede mantener la calidad del agua.
es.typicalValues: Piscinas residenciales: 0.75–2 HP; Velocidad variable: 600–3,450 RPM

terms.definition: A pool pump is the mechanical device that circulates water through the filter, heater, and chlorinator, maintaining water movement and filtration.
terms.explanation: Pool pumps create suction by spinning an impeller that draws water from the skimmer and main drain, pushes it through the filter and other equipment, and returns it to the pool through the return jets. Pump sizing must match the pool volume and plumbing resistance to achieve adequate turnover rate. Variable speed pumps can adjust their speed for energy savings while maintaining adequate circulation.
terms.whyItMatters: The pump is the heart of the pool system. Without adequate circulation, no chemical treatment can maintain water quality.
terms.typicalValues: Residential pools: 0.75–2 HP; Variable speed: 600–3,450 RPM

terms.definition: A DE (diatomaceous earth) filter uses diatomaceous earth powder coated on internal grids to filter pool water to 3–5 micron fineness.
terms.explanation: DE filters consist of a housing with fabric-covered grids. Diatomaceous earth (the fossilized shells of diatoms) is added and coats the grids, creating a very fine filtration surface. Water passes through this DE layer, which captures particles down to 3–5 microns — finer than either sand or cartridge filters. DE filters require periodic backwashing, adding fresh DE powder, and annual disassembly for full cleaning.
terms.whyItMatters: DE filters produce the clearest water of any standard pool filter type but require more maintenance knowledge and attention than sand or cartridge.
terms.typicalValues: Filtration fineness: 3–5 microns; Recharge with DE after backwashing

es.definition: GPM es la unidad que mide el caudal del agua a través de una bomba de piscina u otro equipo.
es.explanation: GPM (galones por minuto) es la especificación clave para dimensionar bombas de piscina y tuberías.
