El GPM de una bomba a una presión de descarga específica del sistema determina qué tan rápido puede lograr una recirculación de la piscina. Las piscinas más grandes requieren bombas de mayor GPM para lograr el mismo tiempo de recirculación. La resistencia de las tuberías (presión de descarga) reduce el GPM real por debajo del máximo teórico de la bomba.
es.whyItMatters: El GPM es la unidad de caudal fundamental usada en el dimensionamiento de bombas, los cálculos de recirculación y las especificaciones de equipo.
es.typicalValues: Piscinas residenciales: 40–80 GPM; Hot tubs: 80–120 GPM (para los chorros)

terms.definition: GPM is the unit measuring the flow rate of water through a pool pump or other equipment.
terms.explanation: GPM (gallons per minute) is the key specification for sizing pool pumps and plumbing. A pump's GPM at a specific system head pressure determines how quickly it can achieve a pool turnover. Larger pools require higher GPM pumps for the same turnover time. Plumbing resistance (head pressure) reduces actual GPM below the pump's theoretical maximum.
terms.whyItMatters: GPM is the fundamental flow rate unit used in pump sizing, turnover calculations, and equipment specifications.
terms.typicalValues: Residential pools: 40–80 GPM; Hot tubs: 80–120 GPM (for jets)

es.definition: El agua agresiva (corrosiva) tiene un LSI por debajo de −0.3, lo que significa que está subsaturada de carbonato de calcio y disolverá minerales de las superficies y el equipo de la piscina.
es.explanation: El agua agresiva ataca el calcio de las superficies de yeso, graba el concreto, corroe el equipo metálico y desgasta la lechada. Las causas principales son el pH bajo, la dureza cálcica baja y la alcalinidad total baja. El agua dulce blanda recién agregada (bajo contenido mineral) es inherentemente agresiva. La solución es subir el pH, la alcalinidad y/o la dureza cálcica hasta que el LSI alcance el rango aceptable de −0.3 a +0.3.
es.whyItMatters: El agua agresiva causa daños permanentes en las superficies y corrosión del equipo. La corrección temprana evita reparaciones costosas.
es.typicalValues: Un LSI por debajo de −0.3 indica agua agresiva; por debajo de −0.5 es preocupante; por debajo de −1.0 es un problema grave

terms.definition: Aggressive (corrosive) water has an LSI below -0.3, meaning it is under-saturated with calcium carbonate and will dissolve minerals from pool surfaces and equipment.
terms.explanation: Aggressive water attacks calcium from plaster surfaces, etches concrete, corrodes metal equipment, and strips grout. The primary causes are low pH, low calcium hardness, and low total alkalinity. Fresh soft water (low mineral content) is inherently aggressive. The fix is raising pH, alkalinity, and/or calcium hardness until the LSI reaches the acceptable range of -0.3 to +0.3.
terms.whyItMatters: Aggressive water causes permanent surface damage and equipment corrosion. Early correction prevents expensive repairs.
terms.typicalValues: LSI below -0.3 indicates aggressive water; below -0.5 is concerning; below -1.0 is a serious problem

es.definition: El agua incrustante tiene un LSI por encima de +0.3, lo que significa que está sobresaturada de carbonato de calcio y depositará incrustaciones en las superficies y el equipo.
es.explanation: El agua sobresaturada deposita carbonato de calcio como incrustaciones cristalinas blancas o grises en las líneas de azulejos, los elementos del calentador, las células salinas, las tuberías y las superficies de la piscina. Las causas principales son el pH alto, la dureza cálcica alta y la temperatura alta. Prevenir las incrustaciones requiere mantener el LSI por debajo de +0.3 mediante la gestión del pH, la gestión de la dureza cálcica y el uso de productos inhibidores de incrustaciones en casos límite.
es.whyItMatters: Las incrustaciones en los elementos del calentador actúan como aislante, causando sobrecalentamiento y fallas prematuras. Las incrustaciones en las células salinas reducen la eficiencia de generación de cloro.
es.typicalValues: Un LSI por encima de +0.3 indica tendencia a formar incrustaciones; por encima de +0.5 es motivo de preocupación

terms.definition: Scaling water has an LSI above +0.3, meaning it is over-saturated with calcium carbonate and will deposit scale on surfaces and equipment.
terms.explanation: Over-saturated water deposits calcium carbonate as white or grey crystalline scale on tile lines, heater elements, salt cells, pipes, and pool surfaces. The primary causes are high pH, high calcium hardness, and high temperature. Preventing scale requires keeping the LSI below +0.3 through pH management, calcium hardness management, and the use of scale inhibitor products in borderline cases.
terms.whyItMatters: Scale deposits on heater elements act as insulation, causing overheating and premature failure. Scale on salt cells reduces chlorine generation efficiency.
terms.typicalValues: LSI above +0.3 indicates scaling tendency; above +0.5 is a concern

terms.definition: Total hardness measures all divalent mineral ions in water (calcium and magnesium), while pool chemistry specifically uses only calcium hardness.
terms.explanation: Total hardness (as used in household water softening) includes both calcium and magnesium hardness. In pool chemistry, only calcium hardness is relevant because calcium is the ion that participates in calcium carbonate equilibrium (and therefore the LSI). Magnesium does not contribute to pool scaling in the same way. When comparing tap water hardness reports (which give total hardness) to pool targets (calcium hardness), note that calcium typically represents 60–70% of total hardness in most water supplies.
terms.whyItMatters: Distinguishing total hardness from calcium hardness prevents miscalculation when using municipal water quality reports for pool chemistry.
terms.typicalValues: Pool targets use calcium hardness; calcium is ~60–70% of total hardness in typical tap water

terms.definition: Phosphates are nutrients present in pool water that can promote algae growth when free chlorine is inadequate.
terms.explanation: Phosphates (orthophosphates and polyphosphates) enter pools from fertiliser runoff, leaves, dust, some municipal water supplies, and certain pool products. They act as a nutrient source for algae. Some pool chemistry systems (particularly in commercial applications) use phosphate removers to reduce algae potential. However, most pool chemistry authorities note that adequate free chlorine is far more important for algae control than phosphate removal.
terms.whyItMatters: High phosphate levels can make algae harder to control, but fixing low free chlorine is always the primary intervention.
terms.typicalValues: Target: below 500 ppb; treat with phosphate remover if above 1,000 ppb and algae is recurring

terms.definition: Iron in pool water is a dissolved metal that can cause reddish-brown staining when oxidised by chlorine or shock treatment.
terms.explanation: Iron enters pool water from well water sources, corroding iron equipment, or certain algaecide products. Dissolved (ferrous) iron is clear in water. When oxidised by chlorine (especially during shock treatment), it converts to ferric iron (rust), which precipitates as a red-brown stain. Adding a metal sequestrant before shocking prevents iron from depositing on pool surfaces.
terms.whyItMatters: Iron staining is one of the most common causes of unexpected brown discolouration in pools, especially after shock treatment.
terms.typicalValues: Acceptable: below 0.2 ppm; Staining risk increases above 0.3 ppm

terms.definition: Copper is a dissolved metal found in some pool water that causes blue-green staining when oxidised.
terms.explanation: Copper enters pool water from copper-based algaecides, corroding copper plumbing (often in aggressive low-pH water), or copper-core pool equipment. At low concentrations, copper is invisible. When shocked with high-concentration chlorine, dissolved copper oxidises and precipitates as blue-green or teal deposits on pool surfaces and hair. Using a metal sequestrant before shock is the standard prevention.
terms.whyItMatters: Copper staining is a common side effect of using copper algaecide in corrosive water (low pH, low hardness). Understanding the cause prevents recurrence.
terms.typicalValues: Staining threshold: approximately 0.5 ppm dissolved copper

terms.definition: Winterization is the process of preparing a pool or hot tub for winter shutdown, including draining, blowing out plumbing lines, and protecting equipment from freeze damage.
terms.explanation: Pool winterization typically involves: lowering the water level below the skimmer, adding winterising chemicals to the remaining water, blowing out all plumbing lines with compressed air, plugging all fittings, installing an air pillow under the cover (to absorb ice expansion), and covering the pool. Hot tub winterization requires fully draining all water from the shell and all plumbing to prevent freeze cracking.
terms.whyItMatters: Incomplete winterization is the most common cause of expensive freeze damage to pool and spa equipment, including cracked pipes and fittings.
terms.typicalValues: Complete winterization required when outdoor temperatures consistently drop below 32°F

es.definition: La dilución se refiere a la reducción en la concentración química del agua de la piscina causada por la adición de agua (lluvia, relleno, salpicaduras).
es.explanation: La dilución reduce todos los productos químicos disueltos de forma proporcional. Una dilución del 10% (reemplazar el 10% del volumen de la piscina con agua nueva) reduce todos los parámetros en un 10%. La dilución es la única forma de reducir el CYA, la dureza cálcica, los sólidos disueltos totales (TDS) y la sal. La dilución por lluvia es significativa después de tormentas fuertes — una lluvia de una pulgada agrega aproximadamente 600 galones de agua con química casi nula por cada 1,000 pies cuadrados de superficie de piscina, lo que puede cambiar significativamente la TA y la dureza en una piscina pequeña.
es.whyItMatters: Comprender la dilución ayuda a explicar por qué los parámetros bajan después de lluvias intensas y por qué los drenajes parciales son la única forma de reducir ciertos parámetros.
es.typicalValues: Porcentaje de dilución = (agua agregada) ÷ (volumen total de la piscina) × 100

terms.definition: Dilution refers to the reduction in chemical concentration in pool water caused by adding water (rain, refill, splash-out).
terms.explanation: Dilution reduces all dissolved chemicals proportionally. A 10% dilution (replacing 10% of pool volume with fresh water) reduces all parameters by 10%. Dilution is the only way to reduce CYA, calcium hardness, TDS, and salt. Rain dilution is significant after heavy storms — a 1-inch rainstorm adds approximately 600 gallons of near-zero-chemistry water per 1,000 square feet of pool surface, which can significantly change TA and hardness in a small pool.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding dilution helps explain why parameters drop after heavy rainfall and why partial drains are the only way to reduce certain parameters.
terms.typicalValues: Dilution percentage = (water added) / (total pool volume) × 100

terms.definition: A multiport valve is the control valve on a sand or DE filter that selects between filter, backwash, rinse, waste, and other operational modes.
terms.explanation: Multiport valves have typically 6 positions: Filter (normal operation), Backwash (reverse flow to clean), Rinse (forward flow to waste to re-seat sand after backwash), Waste (bypass filter, direct flow to waste for vacuuming or draining), Recirculate (circulates without filtering), and Closed. The valve must never be rotated when the pump is running — always turn the pump off first.
terms.whyItMatters: Operating the multiport valve with the pump running causes severe damage to the valve O-ring and face. This is one of the most common causes of filter valve failure.
terms.typicalValues: Always turn pump off before changing valve position

terms.definition: The main drain is the fitting at the lowest point of a pool that allows the pool to be completely drained and provides a second suction point for the pump.
terms.explanation: The main drain allows the pool to be fully drained for maintenance. During normal operation, it shares suction duty with the skimmer, pulling water from the pool bottom to complement the surface skimming. Main drain covers are a safety requirement — they must be anti-entrapment rated (ANSI/ASME A112.19.8) to prevent suction entrapment of hair or body parts. Inspect and replace damaged main drain covers immediately.
terms.whyItMatters: Main drain covers are a life safety item — missing or damaged covers have caused child drownings from suction entrapment.
terms.typicalValues: Anti-entrapment drain covers required; replace if cracked, missing, or improperly secured

terms.definition: Return jets are the fittings in a pool wall through which filtered and treated water is returned to the pool.
terms.explanation: Return jets direct treated water back into the pool, creating circulation that distributes sanitiser and temperature throughout the pool. They should be angled to create a circular current pattern that maximises mixing. Adjustable return jet fittings allow direction control. In pools with poor circulation spots (corners, areas away from returns), algae and sediment tend to accumulate — adjusting return jet angles can improve these areas.
terms.whyItMatters: Return jet positioning affects chemical distribution and circulation dead zones, which are algae-prone areas.
terms.typicalValues: Typically angled 45° toward the surface and directed to create clockwise pool circulation

es.definition: Un índice de saturación es un valor calculado que predice si el agua de la piscina disolverá minerales (índice negativo) o los depositará como incrustaciones (índice positivo).
es.explanation: El Índice de Saturación de Langelier (LSI) es el índice de saturación estándar para el agua de piscina. El Índice de Estabilidad de Ryznar (RSI) es otra versión que usa criterios de interpretación ligeramente distintos. Ambos miden la misma tendencia fundamental del agua a corroer o formar incrustaciones. El LSI es el más utilizado en la industria de piscinas.
es.whyItMatters: Los índices de saturación ofrecen una forma unificada de evaluar el balance del agua, teniendo en cuenta la interacción de todos los parámetros de balance simultáneamente.
es.typicalValues: Objetivo de LSI: −0.3 a +0.3

terms.definition: A saturation index is a calculated value predicting whether pool water will dissolve minerals (negative index) or deposit them as scale (positive index).
terms.explanation: The Langelier Saturation Index (LSI) is the standard saturation index for pool water. The Ryznar Stability Index (RSI) is another version that uses slightly different interpretation criteria. Both measure the same fundamental tendency of water to corrode or scale. The LSI is the more widely used in the pool industry.
terms.whyItMatters: Saturation indices provide a unified way to assess water balance accounting for the interplay of all balance parameters simultaneously.
terms.typicalValues: LSI target: -0.3 to +0.3

terms.definition: Evaporation is the loss of water from a pool's surface as water molecules escape into the air, which concentrates dissolved chemicals and raises TDS.
terms.explanation: Pool evaporation is significant in hot, dry, or windy climates. Evaporation removes pure water but leaves dissolved minerals behind, increasing the concentration of calcium hardness, CYA, TDS, and all other dissolved compounds. A pool in a hot climate can lose 1–2 inches of water per week to evaporation. Refilling maintains volume but does not reduce elevated dissolved mineral concentrations.
terms.whyItMatters: Evaporation explains why pool hardness and TDS increase over a summer season even without adding hardness-related chemicals.
terms.typicalValues: Evaporation rate: 0.5–2 inches per week depending on temperature, humidity, and wind

es.definition: Un drenaje parcial es el proceso de retirar una parte del agua de la piscina y reemplazarla con agua nueva para diluir los compuestos disueltos acumulados.
es.explanation: Los drenajes parciales se usan para reducir el CYA, la dureza cálcica, los TDS y la sal, que no pueden bajarse mediante tratamiento químico. Un drenaje parcial del 25% reduce todos los compuestos disueltos en un 25%. Un drenaje del 50% los reduce en un 50%. Por ejemplo, si el CYA está en 100 ppm y el objetivo es 50 ppm, un drenaje del 50% lo devuelve al objetivo. El agua de relleno nueva típicamente vuelve a aportar una pequeña cantidad de esos compuestos, según la calidad del agua de la llave.
es.whyItMatters: Los drenajes parciales son el único método para reducir el CYA, los TDS y otros compuestos acumulados en el agua de la piscina.
es.typicalValues: Un drenaje parcial del 25% elimina el 25% de todos los compuestos disueltos; el momento depende de la temporada y del motivo

terms.definition: A partial drain is the process of removing a portion of pool water and replacing it with fresh water to dilute accumulated dissolved compounds.
terms.explanation: Partial drains are used to reduce CYA, calcium hardness, TDS, and salt that cannot be lowered by chemical treatment. A 25% partial drain reduces all dissolved compounds by 25%. A 50% drain reduces them by 50%. For example, if CYA is at 100 ppm and the target is 50 ppm, a 50% drain brings it back to the target. The fresh refill water typically adds back a small amount of the compounds depending on the tap water quality.
terms.whyItMatters: Partial drains are the only method for reducing CYA, TDS, and other accumulated compounds in pool water.
terms.typicalValues: 25% partial drain removes 25% of all dissolved compounds; timing depends on season and reason

es.definition: La tasa de recirculación de la piscina es el tiempo requerido para que la bomba haga circular todo el volumen de la piscina a través del sistema de filtración una vez.
es.explanation: Tasa de recirculación = Volumen de la piscina ÷ GPM de la bomba = tiempo para una filtración completa de toda el agua de la piscina. El mínimo de la industria es una recirculación completa cada 8 horas. Las piscinas con alta carga de bañistas se benefician de 2 a 3 recirculaciones por día. Las bombas de velocidad variable permiten tiempos de funcionamiento más largos a caudal reducido, logrando más recirculaciones a un menor costo energético.
es.whyItMatters: La tasa de recirculación determina directamente la calidad del agua. Una recirculación insuficiente es una causa principal de agua turbia persistente y dificultad en la gestión de la química.
es.typicalValues: Mínimo: 8 horas por recirculación; Óptimo: 4–6 horas por recirculación (2–3 veces al día)

terms.definition: Pool turnover rate is the time required for the pool pump to circulate the entire pool volume through the filtration system once.
terms.explanation: Turnover rate = Pool volume / Pump GPM = time for one complete filtration of all pool water. The industry minimum is one complete turnover per 8 hours. Pools with high bather load benefit from 2–3 turnovers per day. Variable speed pumps allow extended run times at reduced flow to achieve more turnovers at lower energy cost.
terms.whyItMatters: Turnover rate directly determines water quality. Insufficient turnover is a leading cause of persistent cloudy water and chemistry management difficulty.
terms.typicalValues: Minimum: 8 hours per turnover; Optimal: 4–6 hours per turnover (2–3x per day)

terms.definition: Pink slime is a pink or orange bacterial growth caused by Serratia marcescens or Methylobacterium species, commonly seen in hot tubs and pool fittings.
terms.explanation: Pink slime is not an algae — it is a bacterial biofilm. It typically appears in wet areas: around hot tub fittings, under cover seals, in tile grout, and around skimmer baskets. It is resistant to normal chlorine levels because it forms a protective slime layer. Treatment requires physical scrubbing to remove the biofilm, followed by shocking the water to 10+ ppm FC.
terms.whyItMatters: Pink slime indicates a biofilm problem that normal maintenance has not addressed. Its presence suggests the sanitiser is not reaching all surfaces effectively.
terms.typicalValues: Treat with scrubbing + shock; check that sanitiser is reaching all affected areas

terms.definition: Water temperature affects chlorine demand, chemical reaction rates, calcium solubility, and the Langelier Saturation Index.
terms.explanation: Chlorine degrades approximately twice as fast for every 10°F increase in water temperature. pH drifts upward faster in warm water due to increased CO2 off-gassing. The LSI increases with temperature, raising the scaling risk. Pool temperature typically ranges from 78–84°F; hot tub temperature from 98–104°F. Testing and chemical management should be adjusted seasonally to account for temperature-driven chemistry changes.
terms.whyItMatters: Temperature is one of the most commonly overlooked variables in pool chemistry management, yet it affects nearly every chemical parameter.
terms.typicalValues: Pool: 78–84°F; Hot tub: 98–104°F; Maximum safe: 104°F

terms.definition: A pressure gauge on the pool filter measures water pressure inside the filter housing in psi, indicating filter cleanliness and flow resistance.
terms.explanation: Record the filter's baseline pressure when the filter is clean. As the filter captures particles over days or weeks of operation, pressure rises. The standard cleaning threshold is 8–10 psi above baseline. A sudden pressure drop (below baseline) can indicate a pump problem, a broken filter element, or an air leak in the suction line. A pressure gauge that is stuck or not responsive should be replaced.
terms.whyItMatters: The pressure gauge is the primary tool for determining when the filter needs cleaning.
terms.typicalValues: Clean: baseline pressure; Backwash/clean needed: baseline + 8–10 psi

terms.definition: Dead algae is killed algae cells that remain suspended or settled in pool water after shock treatment, causing grey or white cloudiness.
terms.explanation: After successfully shocking an algae bloom, the killed algae cells do not disappear — they become fine grey-white particles suspended in the water. This is what causes the characteristic grey-white cloudiness that follows a green pool treatment. Dead algae must be removed by continuous filtration, backwashing or cartridge cleaning, and vacuuming to waste. Adding clarifier can speed up particle aggregation for filter capture.
terms.whyItMatters: Dead algae cloudiness is a normal part of algae recovery — it indicates the treatment worked, not that there is a new problem.
terms.typicalValues: Clears within 12–48 hours of continuous filtration after successful shock treatment

es.definition: Un kit químico de apertura de piscina es un paquete de productos químicos preparado para la apertura de la piscina en primavera, que típicamente incluye choque, alguicida y prevención de manchas.
es.explanation: Los kits de apertura suelen contener: cloro de choque (hipoclorito de calcio), alguicida (dosis inicial), inhibidor de manchas e incrustaciones, y a veces un clarificador y tiras de prueba. Ofrecen un punto de partida conveniente para la química de la temporada de apertura, pero no deben sustituir un análisis completo del agua — las necesidades químicas reales dependen por completo de la química del agua con la que se está abriendo la piscina.
es.whyItMatters: Los kits de apertura son un producto de conveniencia. Usar uno sin analizar primero el agua puede llevar a agregar productos que no se necesitan y a omitir ajustes que sí se necesitan.
es.typicalValues: Úselo como punto de partida; verifique todos los parámetros con un análisis de agua antes y después de la apertura

terms.definition: A pool opening chemical kit is a package of chemicals assembled for spring pool opening, typically including shock, algaecide, and stain prevention.
terms.explanation: Opening kits typically contain: shock chlorine (calcium hypochlorite), algaecide (initial dose), stain and scale inhibitor, and sometimes a clarifier and test strips. They provide a convenient starting point for opening season chemistry but should not substitute for a full water test — the actual chemical needs depend entirely on the chemistry of the water you are opening with.
terms.whyItMatters: Opening kits are a convenience product. Using one without testing first can lead to adding chemicals that are not needed and missing adjustments that are.
terms.typicalValues: Use as a starting point; verify all parameters with a water test before and after opening

es.definition: Un kit químico de cierre de piscina contiene los productos químicos necesarios para balancear y proteger el agua de la piscina durante el reposo invernal.
es.explanation: Los kits de cierre suelen incluir: choque, alguicida (fórmula de invierno), inhibidor de manchas, y a veces un dispensador flotante de cloro. El objetivo es dejar la piscina en reposo con agua balanceada que resista las algas y las incrustaciones durante meses de inactividad. La invernización requiere un balance correcto de pH y alcalinidad, una dosis de alguicida, y suficiente cloro para mantener un residual durante varias semanas.
es.whyItMatters: Un cierre químico adecuado evita brotes severos de algas que de otro modo se desarrollarían durante el invierno, y que requerirían una costosa recuperación en primavera.
es.typicalValues: Analice y balancee la química por completo antes de agregar los productos del kit de cierre

terms.definition: A pool closing chemical kit contains the chemicals needed to balance and protect pool water during winter dormancy.
terms.explanation: Closing kits typically include: shock, algaecide (winter formula), stain inhibitor, and sometimes a floating chlorine dispenser. The goal is to put the pool to sleep with balanced water that will resist algae and scale during months of inactivity. Winterising requires correct pH and alkalinity balance, an algaecide dose, and enough chlorine to maintain a residual for several weeks.
terms.whyItMatters: Proper chemical closing prevents severe algae blooms that would otherwise develop over winter, requiring costly spring recovery.
terms.typicalValues: Test and balance chemistry completely before adding closing kit chemicals

terms.definition: Chemical compatibility refers to the safety of mixing or sequentially adding pool chemicals to water without dangerous reactions.
terms.explanation: Most pool chemicals must never be mixed directly. Chlorine and acid (muriatic acid) react to produce chlorine gas — potentially lethal. Chlorine shock and trichlor tablets in contact can ignite. All chemicals should be pre-dissolved separately in fresh water and added to the pool at different locations at different times. Never mix chemicals in the same bucket.
terms.whyItMatters: Mixing incompatible pool chemicals has caused serious injuries and deaths. Storage and handling protocols are safety-critical.
terms.typicalValues: Always add chemicals separately; wait at least 30 minutes between additions

terms.definition: Carbon dioxide (CO2) in pool water forms carbonic acid, which influences pH and contributes to the natural downward pH drift in some systems.
terms.explanation: Dissolved CO2 acts as a weak acid in water. Pools with high aeration (waterfalls, fountains, spa jets) off-gas CO2 rapidly, which raises pH as the acidic CO2 leaves the water. Conversely, adding CO2 gas (through a CO2 injection system) is an alternative to muriatic acid for pH control in commercial pools — it is safer and provides precise pH management. The relationship between CO2, pH, and alkalinity is central to water balance chemistry.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding CO2 off-gassing explains why aerated pools and hot tubs consistently drift toward high pH.
terms.typicalValues: Naturally present; off-gassing rate increases with temperature and agitation

terms.definition: Ammonia in pool water is the primary nitrogen source for chloramine formation, introduced by bather waste including sweat and urine.
terms.explanation: Ammonia (NH3) reacts with free chlorine to form chloramines — the source of pool odour and eye irritation. Every swimmer introduces approximately 70 mg of urea (which converts to ammonia) per hour of swimming. The presence of significant ammonia in pool water is a sign of high bather load without adequate free chlorine to react with and neutralise it before it forms chloramines.
terms.whyItMatters: Ammonia input from bathers is unavoidable. Managing chlorine levels to stay ahead of ammonia input prevents chloramine accumulation.
terms.typicalValues: No target value — ammonia should be consumed by free chlorine before it accumulates

es.definition: La conductividad es una medida de la capacidad del agua para conducir electricidad, que aumenta con la concentración de iones disueltos.
es.explanation: Un TDS más alto en el agua de la piscina aumenta la conductividad eléctrica. En piscinas salinas, la conductividad es una medida secundaria de la concentración de sal. Algunos dispositivos digitales de análisis de agua miden la conductividad como indicador indirecto del TDS o del nivel de sal. La conductividad se mide en microsiemens por centímetro (µS/cm) o milisiemens por centímetro (mS/cm). Los medidores de sal de las piscinas salinas a menudo en realidad miden la conductividad y convierten la lectura en una concentración estimada de sal.
es.whyItMatters: Los medidores de sal basados en conductividad son comunes en las piscinas salinas. Comprender cómo funcionan ayuda a interpretar sus lecturas correctamente.
es.typicalValues: Objetivo en piscina salina: aproximadamente 5,000–6,000 µS/cm (corresponde a ~3,000–3,400 ppm de sal)

terms.definition: Conductivity is a measure of water's ability to conduct electricity, which increases with the concentration of dissolved ions.
terms.explanation: Higher TDS in pool water increases electrical conductivity. In salt pools, conductivity is a secondary measure of salt concentration. Some digital water testing devices measure conductivity as a proxy for TDS or salt level. Conductivity is measured in microsiemens per centimeter (µS/cm) or millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). Salt pool salt meters often actually measure conductivity and convert the reading to estimated salt concentration.
terms.whyItMatters: Conductivity-based salt meters are common in salt pools. Understanding how they work helps interpret their readings correctly.
terms.typicalValues: Salt pool target: approximately 5,000–6,000 µS/cm (corresponds to ~3,000–3,400 ppm salt)

es.definition: La dosis de choque se refiere a la cantidad de producto de choque necesaria para elevar el cloro libre al nivel objetivo, según el volumen de la piscina y el objetivo del tratamiento.
es.explanation: El choque de mantenimiento estándar eleva el FC a 10 ppm. El choque de recuperación para piscinas verdes apunta a 30 ppm. La dosis depende de: el volumen de la piscina (en galones), el aumento objetivo de FC (en ppm), y el porcentaje de cloro disponible del producto. Use la calculadora de choque para piscina para calcular la dosis exacta. Predisuelva el choque granular en un balde de agua antes de agregarlo a la piscina.
es.whyItMatters: Una dosis de choque insuficiente no alcanza el punto de ruptura y desperdicia producto. Una dosis excesiva retrasa el reingreso y agrega calcio innecesario (en el caso del cal-hipo).
es.typicalValues: Mantenimiento: 1 lb de cal-hipo por cada 10,000 gal sube el FC en ~6.5 ppm; Piscina verde: se necesitan varias dosis

terms.definition: Shock dosage refers to the amount of shock product required to raise free chlorine to the target level for the pool volume and treatment goal.
terms.explanation: Standard maintenance shock raises FC to 10 ppm. Recovery shock for green pools targets 30 ppm. The dosage depends on: pool volume (in gallons), the target FC increase (in ppm), and the available chlorine percentage of the product. Use the pool shock calculator to calculate the exact dose. Pre-dissolve granular shock in a bucket of water before adding to the pool.
terms.whyItMatters: Under-dosing shock fails to reach breakpoint and wastes product. Over-dosing delays re-entry and adds unnecessary calcium (for cal-hypo).
terms.typicalValues: Maintenance: 1 lb cal-hypo per 10,000 gal raises FC by ~6.5 ppm; Green pool: multiple doses needed

es.definition: Una referencia de volumen de piscina es una tabla precalculada de volúmenes aproximados para dimensiones comunes de piscina, usada para una estimación rápida de dosis.
es.explanation: Las referencias de volumen de piscina permiten estimaciones rápidas sin realizar el cálculo completo. Una piscina de 12×24 pies con 5 pies de profundidad promedio contiene aproximadamente 10,800 galones. Una piscina de 16×32 pies a 5 pies contiene aproximadamente 19,200 galones. Estos valores de referencia deben verificarse contra las dimensiones reales de la piscina para una dosificación química precisa.
es.whyItMatters: Las referencias rápidas de volumen ayudan a los propietarios de piscinas a tomar decisiones de dosificación inmediatas cuando no pueden medir la piscina con precisión.
es.typicalValues: Piscina común: 10,000–25,000 galones; Hot tubs: 250–500 galones

terms.definition: A pool volume reference is a pre-calculated table of approximate volumes for common pool dimensions, used for quick dose estimation.
terms.explanation: Pool volume references allow quick estimates without running the full calculation. A 12×24 foot pool with 5 ft average depth holds approximately 10,800 gallons. A 16×32 foot pool at 5 ft holds approximately 19,200 gallons. These reference values should be verified against the actual pool dimensions for precise chemical dosing.
terms.whyItMatters: Quick volume references help pool owners make immediate dosing decisions when they cannot measure the pool precisely.
terms.typicalValues: Common pool: 10,000–25,000 gallons; Hot tubs: 250–500 gallons

terms.definition: Bicarbonate alkalinity is the portion of total alkalinity contributed by bicarbonate ions (HCO3-), which is the dominant form in properly maintained pool water.
terms.explanation: Total alkalinity in pool water (at pH 7.2–7.6) consists predominantly of bicarbonate ions. Carbonate and hydroxide alkalinity are negligible at normal pool pH. When a test kit measures total alkalinity, it is effectively measuring bicarbonate alkalinity in a well-maintained pool. Sodium bicarbonate additions directly increase bicarbonate alkalinity.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding that pool alkalinity is primarily bicarbonate alkalinity explains the chemistry of sodium bicarbonate additions and acid-based reductions.
terms.typicalValues: At pool pH range (7.2–7.6), >95% of total alkalinity is bicarbonate alkalinity

es.definition: El pH saturado (pHs) es el pH teórico al cual el agua de la piscina estaría exactamente en equilibrio con el carbonato de calcio, usado en el cálculo del LSI.
es.explanation: El pHs es el pH al cual el agua está exactamente saturada de carbonato de calcio, dada su temperatura, dureza cálcica y alcalinidad actuales. El LSI se calcula como: LSI = pH − pHs. Si el pH real está por encima del pHs, el agua está sobresaturada (LSI positivo). Si está por debajo, subsaturada (LSI negativo). El pHs se calcula a partir de la temperatura, la dureza cálcica y la alcalinidad total.
es.whyItMatters: El pHs es el concepto central en el cálculo del LSI. Comprenderlo muestra por qué subir el pH a 7.8 en agua tibia y dura crea un riesgo grave de incrustaciones.
es.typicalValues: pHs para piscinas típicas: 7.5–8.0 según la dureza, la alcalinidad y la temperatura

terms.definition: Saturated pH (pHs) is the theoretical pH at which pool water would be exactly in equilibrium with calcium carbonate, used in LSI calculation.
terms.explanation: pHs is the pH at which water is exactly saturated with calcium carbonate given its current temperature, calcium hardness, and alkalinity. The LSI is calculated as: LSI = pH - pHs. If the actual pH is above pHs, the water is over-saturated (positive LSI). If below, under-saturated (negative LSI). The pHs is calculated from temperature, calcium hardness, and total alkalinity.
terms.whyItMatters: pHs is the central concept in LSI calculation. Understanding it shows why raising pH to 7.8 in warm, hard water creates a severe scaling risk.
terms.typicalValues: pHs for typical pools: 7.5–8.0 depending on hardness, alkalinity, and temperature

es.term: Lista de Verificación de Balance del Agua
es.definition: Una lista de verificación de balance del agua es una secuencia de pruebas y ajustes que asegura que todos los parámetros de la química de la piscina se lleven al rango en el orden correcto.
es.explanation: Una lista de verificación de balance del agua típicamente cubre: 1) Analizar todos los parámetros. 2) Ajustar la alcalinidad total a 80–120 ppm. 3) Volver a analizar y ajustar el pH a 7.2–7.6. 4) Ajustar la dureza cálcica al rango. 5) Ajustar el cloro y el CYA al objetivo. 6) Calcular y verificar el LSI. 7) Documentar todas las pruebas y adiciones. Seguir la lista evita el error común de agregar varios productos químicos al mismo tiempo o en el orden incorrecto.
es.whyItMatters: Una lista de verificación escrita asegura que no se omita nada y que los ajustes se realicen en la secuencia correcta.
es.typicalValues: TA → pH → CH → FC/CYA (este orden)

terms.definition: A water balance checklist is a sequential list of tests and adjustments that ensures all pool chemistry parameters are brought into range in the correct order.
terms.explanation: A water balance checklist typically covers: 1) Test all parameters. 2) Adjust total alkalinity to 80–120 ppm. 3) Test again and adjust pH to 7.2–7.6. 4) Adjust calcium hardness to range. 5) Adjust chlorine and CYA to target. 6) Calculate and check LSI. 7) Document all tests and additions. Following the checklist prevents the common mistake of adding multiple chemicals simultaneously or in the wrong order.
terms.whyItMatters: A written checklist ensures nothing is missed and that adjustments are made in the correct sequence.
terms.typicalValues: TA → pH → CH → FC/CYA (this order)

es.definition: Una referencia de química de piscina es una tabla compilada de rangos objetivo, valores típicos y guías de ajuste para todos los parámetros principales del agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: Las referencias de química de piscina compilan los rangos objetivo de FC (1–3 ppm), pH (7.2–7.6), TA (80–120 ppm), CH (200–400 ppm para yeso), CYA (30–50 ppm), sal (2,700–3,400 ppm) y otros parámetros en un solo formato de referencia rápida. También indican qué producto químico usar para subir o bajar cada parámetro.
es.whyItMatters: Una guía de referencia física o digital cerca de la piscina permite tomar decisiones rápidas sin tener que recordar todos los rangos objetivo.
es.typicalValues: Resume todos los objetivos de parámetros en un solo lugar

terms.definition: A pool chemistry reference is a compiled table of target ranges, typical values, and adjustment guides for all major pool water parameters.
terms.explanation: Pool chemistry references compile the target ranges for FC (1–3 ppm), pH (7.2–7.6), TA (80–120 ppm), CH (200–400 ppm for plaster), CYA (30–50 ppm), salt (2,700–3,400 ppm), and other parameters into a single quick-reference format. They also indicate the chemical to use for raising or lowering each parameter.
terms.whyItMatters: A physical or digital reference guide kept near the pool allows quick decisions without having to remember all target ranges.
terms.typicalValues: Summarises all parameter targets in one place

terms.definition: A chemical log is a written or digital record of every pool water test result and chemical addition, used for maintenance tracking and liability documentation.
terms.explanation: A good chemical log records: date and time, all test results (FC, TC, CC, pH, TA, CH, CYA), any chemical additions (product, amount, time), equipment status notes, and any unusual observations. For vacation rentals and commercial pools, logs are a legal protection tool and often a regulatory requirement. Retain logs for at least 3 years.
terms.whyItMatters: Chemical logs provide evidence of responsible pool management and help identify patterns that lead to recurring chemistry problems.
terms.typicalValues: Test at minimum twice weekly; record every chemical addition

es.definition: Un calendario de choque para piscina es la frecuencia y el momento planificados de los tratamientos de choque a lo largo de la temporada de natación.
es.explanation: Un calendario de choque típico: aplique choque una vez por semana, la misma noche (después de que la bomba haya funcionado durante el día para la distribución química, y antes de la noche cuando no hay UV). Aplique choque de inmediato después de cualquier carga alta de bañistas, tormenta, o una lectura de cloro combinado por encima de 0.5 ppm. Use de 1 a 2 lb de cal-hipo por cada 10,000 galones para el mantenimiento semanal; dosis más altas para situaciones de recuperación.
es.whyItMatters: Un calendario de choque regular evita la acumulación de cloraminas y detecta problemas de química antes de que se conviertan en emergencias.
es.typicalValues: Mantenimiento semanal: choque hasta 10 ppm de FC; Recuperación de emergencia: choque hasta 30 ppm de FC

terms.definition: A pool shock schedule is the planned frequency and timing of pool shock treatments throughout the swimming season.
terms.explanation: A typical shock schedule: shock once per week on the same night (after the pump has run during the day for chemical distribution, and before the evening when UV is absent). Shock immediately after any heavy bather load, storm, or combined chlorine reading above 0.5 ppm. Use 1–2 lbs of cal-hypo per 10,000 gallons for weekly maintenance; higher doses for recovery situations.
terms.whyItMatters: A regular shock schedule prevents chloramine accumulation and catches chemistry problems before they become emergencies.
terms.typicalValues: Weekly maintenance: shock to 10 ppm FC; Emergency recovery: shock to 30 ppm FC

terms.definition: A water test log is a record sheet for documenting pool or hot tub water test results over time.
terms.explanation: A water test log is the physical or digital record of all water test results. It enables trend analysis — seeing how chemistry changes over time, after certain weather events, or with different usage patterns. A complete log showing consistent, timely testing and corrective action is the best evidence of responsible pool management.
terms.whyItMatters: Logs enable pattern recognition and provide documentation for rental property liability protection.
terms.typicalValues: Log every test: date, time, FC, pH, TA, CH, and any chemicals added

terms.definition: A pool maintenance schedule is a written plan covering daily, weekly, monthly, and seasonal maintenance tasks for pool chemistry and equipment.
terms.explanation: A comprehensive maintenance schedule lists: daily checks (water level, pump running), twice-weekly tasks (FC and pH testing), weekly tasks (shock, brush, skim, empty skimmer), monthly tasks (full chemistry test, filter cleaning), and seasonal tasks (opening, peak season adjustment, closing). Having a written schedule prevents missed tasks and distributes maintenance work throughout the season.
terms.whyItMatters: A maintenance schedule prevents the "out of sight, out of mind" neglect that causes most pool chemistry emergencies.
terms.typicalValues: FC/pH: 2x weekly; Full test: monthly; Shock: weekly; Filter clean: monthly

es.definition: La dosis de ruptura es la cantidad específica de cloro libre que debe agregarse para destruir todo el cloro combinado en el agua de la piscina.
es.explanation: Dosis de ruptura = 10 × (lectura de cloro combinado en ppm). Si el CC = 0.8 ppm, la dosis de ruptura = 8 ppm de FC adicional. El nivel actual de FC debe sumarse a la dosis de ruptura para determinar el FC objetivo total: si el FC actual es 1.5 ppm y la dosis de ruptura es 8 ppm, el FC objetivo = 9.5 ppm. La calculadora de choque no acepta una lectura de cloro combinado ni calcula este objetivo por sí misma — seleccione el valor preestablecido disponible más cercano (5, 10, 15 o 20 ppm) para su producto, o aplique directamente la fórmula de dosis de choque para obtener una cifra exacta.
es.whyItMatters: Calcular la dosis de ruptura exacta evita la subdosificación (que no logra destruir las cloraminas y desperdicia producto) y la sobredosificación (que extiende el tiempo de espera para el reingreso).
es.typicalValues: Dosis de ruptura = 10 × CC; típico: 5–15 ppm de FC adicional

terms.definition: The breakpoint dose is the specific amount of free chlorine that must be added to destroy all combined chlorine in pool water.
terms.explanation: Breakpoint dose = 10 × (combined chlorine reading in ppm). If CC = 0.8 ppm, breakpoint dose = 8 ppm of additional FC. The current FC level must be added to the breakpoint dose to determine the total target FC: if current FC is 1.5 ppm and breakpoint dose is 8 ppm, target FC = 9.5 ppm. The shock calculator does not accept a combined-chlorine reading or compute this target itself -- select the closest available preset (5, 10, 15, or 20 ppm) for your product, or apply the shock dose formula directly for an exact figure.
terms.whyItMatters: Calculating the exact breakpoint dose prevents under-dosing (which fails to destroy chloramines and wastes product) and over-dosing (which extends re-entry wait time).
terms.typicalValues: Breakpoint dose = 10 × CC; typical: 5–15 ppm of additional FC

terms.definition: A colorimetric test measures water chemistry by observing the colour change of a reagent added to a water sample.
terms.explanation: All standard liquid pool tests (DPD, phenol red, etc.) are colorimetric tests — they rely on colour comparison between a treated sample and a reference standard. The colour intensity or shade corresponds to the concentration of the measured parameter. Colorimetric tests can be read visually (using a comparator block) or quantitatively with a photometer, which measures light absorbance through the sample rather than relying on human colour perception.
terms.whyItMatters: Understanding colorimetric testing helps users recognise why lighting conditions, reagent age, and technique affect result accuracy.
terms.typicalValues: Best read in natural light or bright white light; compare immediately after adding reagents

terms.definition: Chemical storage refers to the safe storage of pool and spa chemicals to prevent degradation, accidents, and dangerous reactions.
terms.explanation: Pool chemicals must be stored: in original, sealed containers; in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from heat sources and direct sunlight; away from each other (chlorine and acid must be stored separately); away from flammable materials; in locked storage inaccessible to children and guests. Liquid chlorine degrades faster when stored in hot locations — store in a cool, shaded area and use within 60 days.
terms.whyItMatters: Improper chemical storage causes degradation (reducing effectiveness), fires (chlorine + flammables), and toxic gas generation (chlorine + acid).
terms.typicalValues: Store away from heat; separate chlorine from acid; secure against unauthorised access

terms.definition: Pool safety equipment includes the physical devices required to assist in pool emergency response: life ring, reaching pole, first aid kit, and emergency signage.
terms.explanation: Minimum pool safety equipment includes: a US Coast Guard-approved ring buoy with at least 50 ft of rope, mounted at the pool edge; a reaching pole (shepherd's crook) at least 12 ft long; a first aid kit with current supplies; and a visible CPR instruction placard. These items must be accessible without entering the pool area and should be checked regularly for damage or missing components.
terms.whyItMatters: In a drowning emergency, response time is critical. Immediately available safety equipment makes the difference between a rescue and a fatality.
terms.typicalValues: Required for all vacation rental pools; verify at every guest turnover

es.definition: El elevador de pH es un producto para piscina que sube el pH del agua, típicamente carbonato de sodio (carbonato de sosa) o bicarbonato de sodio.
es.explanation: El elevador de pH (carbonato de sosa) se usa cuando el pH de la piscina cae por debajo de 7.2. El carbonato de sodio (Na2CO3) sube el pH rápidamente con un aumento modesto de la alcalinidad. El bicarbonato de sodio sube principalmente la alcalinidad y, en segundo lugar, el pH — se usa cuando ambos necesitan subir. Predisuélvalo en agua antes de agregarlo a la piscina para evitar la turbidez blanquecina. Agréguelo cerca de los retornos con la bomba en funcionamiento y vuelva a analizar después de 2 a 4 horas.
es.whyItMatters: Un pH bajo (por debajo de 7.2) reduce la comodidad del cloro, corroe las superficies e irrita a los bañistas. Una corrección pronta con elevador de pH es importante.
es.typicalValues: Sube el pH aproximadamente 0.2 por libra por cada 10,000 galones; disuélvalo antes de agregarlo

terms.definition: pH increaser is a pool product that raises water pH, typically sodium carbonate (soda ash) or sodium bicarbonate.
terms.explanation: pH increaser (soda ash) is used when pool pH falls below 7.2. Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) raises pH quickly with a modest alkalinity increase. Sodium bicarbonate raises alkalinity primarily and pH secondarily — it is used when both need raising. Pre-dissolve in water before adding to the pool to prevent white cloudiness. Add near the return jets with the pump running and retest after 2–4 hours.
terms.whyItMatters: Low pH (below 7.2) reduces chlorine comfort, corrodes surfaces, and irritates swimmers. Prompt correction with pH increaser is important.
terms.typicalValues: Raises pH by approximately 0.2 per pound per 10,000 gallons; dissolve before adding
